When a purchase order line's price, quantity or unit of measure changes, run a full revaluation of every valued movement of that line.
When a landed cost is validated, run a full revaluation of every movement named by its adjustment lines.
When a valuation history record is created for a movement, run a full revaluation of that movement.
records.formula: correction_quantity = Σ over the lines of the outgoing movement not excluded for valuation of ( new_line_quantity − old_line_quantity ) ; every other listed event runs a full revaluation with no correction quantity

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the choice itself; the correction quantity is compared at the precision of the unit of measure.
rounding.precision: The Product Unit decimal precision for the correction quantity.
rounding.method: Half away from zero on the quantity.
rounding.step: When the deltas are summed, before the correction quantity is handed to the routine.

result.name: the call to run, and the correction quantity when there is one
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product for the correction quantity
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it selects which computation writes the movement's value.

edge_cases.case: A line is edited on an incoming movement.
edge_cases.outcome: A full revaluation runs, so a receipt always reflects the newest bill, order price and landed cost.

edge_cases.case: A line is edited on an outgoing movement.
edge_cases.outcome: The existing value is scaled, so the first in first out stack is not consumed a second time.

edge_cases.case: A line excluded for valuation is edited on an outgoing movement.
edge_cases.outcome: Its delta is not summed, so the correction quantity ignores it.

edge_cases.case: An event outside the list occurs.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing revalues the movement; its stored value stands.

worked_examples.description: Two lines of a delivery edited, one from six to seven units and one from four to five units
worked_examples.narrative: The deltas are one and one, so the correction quantity is two. The new movement quantity is twelve and the previous quantity is ten, so the value is scaled from 100.00 to 120.00.

records.name: Maintaining the product unit cost: the dispatch
records.purpose: Brings the unit cost of every product touched by a valuation up to date, sending each product to the path its costing method and its lot valuation require, and never creating a valuation history record while doing so.

operands.name: set of products
operands.source: the products-to-recompute collection built by the valuation routine, or a costing method change
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: extra value map
operands.source: the valuation routine, when the incremental fast path is enabled
operands.constraints: absent when an outgoing movement was valued in the same completion

operands.name: extra quantity map
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure per product
operands.source: the valuation routine, when the incremental fast path is enabled
operands.constraints: absent under the same condition

preconditions.condition: The set of products is not empty.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is recomputed.

preconditions.condition: Each product's costing method is known, from its category or from the company fallback.
preconditions.otherwise: The product cannot be grouped and its cost is left unchanged.

procedure: Take each product of the set in turn.

When the product is valuated by lot and its costing method is not `standard`, set its unit cost to its computed average cost, write with elevated privileges and the flag that disables automatic revaluation, and skip the rest for that product, because its cost is an aggregate of its lots' costs.
Otherwise put the product in the group of its costing method.
For the standard price group, do nothing, because the cost is an input.

For the two other groups, when the extra maps were supplied, apply the incremental fast path to the products that appear in the extra value map, scoped to the current company and to the valued perimeter, and remove them from their group.
For the products of the first in first out group that remain, apply the full first in first out path.

For the products of the average cost group that remain, replay the average over the whole set with the recomputation forced and write the resulting unit cost onto each product the replay produced a figure for.
Write every unit cost with the flag that disables automatic revaluation, so that the engine's own recomputations never create valuation history records.
records.formula: unit_cost( product ) = the figure produced by the path the product's costing method and lot valuation select

rounding.what: The unit cost written on each product.
rounding.precision: None on storage: the unit cost is stored at full floating precision and displayed at the Product Price decimal precision.
rounding.method: Not applicable on storage; half away from zero on display.
rounding.step: At display time only.

result.name: unit cost of each product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the product's unit cost field at full floating precision, displayed at the Product Price decimal precision.

edge_cases.case: A product is valuated by lot and uses standard price.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not sent to the lot branch; it goes to the standard price group, where nothing happens.

edge_cases.case: A product appears in the extra value map but an outgoing movement was valued in the same completion.
edge_cases.outcome: The maps are not supplied at all, so the full path runs for every product.

edge_cases.case: The write is initiated by the engine.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag that disables automatic revaluation is set, so no valuation history record is created; only a human's write creates one.

edge_cases.case: The set contains products of several costing methods.
edge_cases.outcome: Each group is handled by its own path within the same call.

worked_examples.description: A completion touching one average-cost product with the fast path enabled and one first in first out product
worked_examples.narrative: The average-cost product takes the incremental fast path: the previous quantity is twenty minus ten, which is ten, so the new unit cost is ten multiplied by 10.00 plus 120.00, all divided by twenty, which is 11.00. The first in first out product takes total value divided by quantity on hand, 1 799.00 divided by one hundred and sixteen, which is 15.508620…. Neither write creates a valuation history record.

records.name: Unit cost of a product valuated by lot
records.purpose: Sets the unit cost of a product whose stock is valued lot by lot to the aggregate of its lots' costs, so that the product-level figure agrees with the sum of its lots.

operands.name: computed average cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the aggregate of the costs of the product's lots inside the valued perimeter
operands.constraints: may be zero when no lot holds stock

preconditions.condition: The product is valuated by lot.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the costing method paths applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The costing method of the product is not `standard`.
preconditions.otherwise: The product goes to the standard price group, where nothing happens and the cost keeps whatever value it had.

procedure: Read the product's computed average cost, which aggregates the costs of its lots.
Write it onto the product's unit cost with elevated privileges and the flag that disables automatic revaluation.
Skip the remaining paths for that product.
records.formula: unit_cost( product ) = computed_average_cost( product ) , the aggregate of the costs of its lots

rounding.what: The unit cost written on the product.
rounding.precision: None on storage: full floating precision.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: unit cost of the product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the product's unit cost field with automatic revaluation disabled.

edge_cases.case: The product holds no lot with stock.
edge_cases.outcome: The computed average cost is zero and the unit cost becomes zero.

edge_cases.case: The product uses standard price and is valuated by lot.
edge_cases.outcome: This branch does not apply; the cost stays as the operator set it.

edge_cases.case: A lot's cost changes.
edge_cases.outcome: The product's unit cost is recomputed the next time the lot is touched by a valuation.

worked_examples.description: A product valuated by lot holding two lots, six units at 10.00 and four units at 12.00
worked_examples.narrative: The lots hold 60.00 and 48.00 for ten units in total, so the aggregate is 108.00 divided by ten, which is 10.80.

records.name: Unit cost under standard price
records.purpose: States that the unit cost of a product using standard price is an input that no recomputation touches, which is what makes the standard price stable between deliberate changes.

operands.name: unit cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: a human's write, the product creation hook or the installation hook
operands.constraints: may be zero

preconditions.condition: The costing method of the product is `standard`.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other paths applies.

preconditions.condition: The product is not valuated by lot, or it is valuated by lot and uses standard price.
preconditions.otherwise: The lot branch applies instead, which does not run under standard price.

procedure: Take no action: the unit cost is an input and the recomputation leaves it exactly as it stands.
records.formula: unit_cost( product ) = unit_cost( product ) , unchanged

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded, because nothing is written.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: unit cost of the product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: Left on the product's unit cost field unchanged.

edge_cases.case: A human writes a new unit cost.
edge_cases.outcome: A valuation history record is created, because the write did not come from the engine, and the new cost governs every later movement.

edge_cases.case: Movements complete for the product.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit cost does not move; the total value is quantity on hand multiplied by the unit cost, exactly.

edge_cases.case: The product moves to a category using standard price.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost keeps whatever value it had at the moment of the change and stops moving.

worked_examples.description: A standard-price product after a receipt of ten units
worked_examples.narrative: The receipt does not change the cost; the unit cost stays 10.00 and the 20.00 difference between the bill and the standard cost is handled by the price difference mechanism.

records.name: The incremental fast path for the unit cost under average cost and first in first out
records.purpose: Updates the unit cost from the receipt just completed instead of replaying the whole history, which is what makes an ordinary receipt cheap while producing the same figure as a full replay.

operands.name: current quantity on hand
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the product's quantity in the valued perimeter of the current company, after the receipt
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: added quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the extra quantity map, being the valued quantity of the incoming movements just valued
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: added value
operands.source: the extra value map, being the value of the incoming movements just valued
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: old unit cost
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product's unit cost before this call
operands.constraints: may be zero

preconditions.condition: The extra value map and the extra quantity map were supplied, which happens only when no outgoing movement was valued in the same completion.
preconditions.otherwise: The full path runs instead.

preconditions.condition: The product appears in the extra value map and is inside the valued perimeter of the current company.
preconditions.otherwise: The product goes to the full path of its costing method.

procedure: Compute the previous quantity as the current quantity on hand minus the added quantity.

When the previous quantity is greater than zero and the current quantity on hand is greater than zero, set the new unit cost to the previous quantity multiplied by the old unit cost plus the added value, all divided by the current quantity on hand.
Otherwise, when the added quantity is not zero, set the new unit cost to the added value divided by the added quantity.
Otherwise leave the unit cost unchanged.
Write the new unit cost with the flag that disables automatic revaluation and remove the product from its costing method group.
records.formula: previous_quantity = current_quantity_on_hand − added_quantity ; new_unit_cost = ( previous_quantity × old_unit_cost + added_value ) ÷ current_quantity_on_hand when previous_quantity > 0 and current_quantity_on_hand > 0 ; new_unit_cost = added_value ÷ added_quantity when the first case does not apply and added_quantity ≠ 0 ; no change when neither case applies

rounding.precision: None on storage: full floating precision; the Product Price decimal precision on display.
rounding.method: Half away from zero on display.
rounding.step: At display time only; the division is not rounded before storage.

result.name: unit cost of the product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the product's unit cost field with automatic revaluation disabled.

edge_cases.case: The previous quantity is zero, because the product had nothing on hand.
edge_cases.outcome: The second case applies and the cost becomes the added value divided by the added quantity, so the receipt sets the cost outright.

edge_cases.case: The previous quantity is negative, because stock was negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The second case applies and the cost is taken from the arriving goods alone.

edge_cases.case: The added quantity is zero and the first case does not apply.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing changes.

edge_cases.case: The current quantity on hand is zero after the receipt.
edge_cases.outcome: The first case does not apply, so the cost is taken from the arriving goods alone when the added quantity is not zero.

edge_cases.case: An outgoing movement was valued in the same completion.
edge_cases.outcome: The fast path is not enabled at all, because it assumes the quantity on hand moved only by the incoming amount.

worked_examples.description: Ten units on hand at 10.00 receiving ten more valued at 120.00
worked_examples.narrative: The previous quantity is twenty minus ten, which is ten. Ten multiplied by 10.00 is 100.00, plus the added value of 120.00 is 220.00, divided by the current quantity on hand of twenty gives 11.00.

worked_examples.description: Nothing on hand at a cost of 10.00 receiving ten units valued at 120.00
worked_examples.narrative: The previous quantity is zero, so the first case does not apply. The added quantity is ten, so the new unit cost is 120.00 divided by ten, which is 12.00.

records.name: The full path for the unit cost under first in first out
records.purpose: Reports a unit cost for a product valued first in first out, where the cost is a reporting figure derived from the value actually held rather than a driver of the valuation.

operands.name: quantity on hand in the valued perimeter
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the product's quantity inside the valued perimeter of the current company
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: total value of the product
operands.source: the first in first out valuation of the quantity on hand
operands.constraints: may be negative when stock is negative

operands.name: unit price of the most recent incoming movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the last incoming movement of the product
operands.constraints: may be zero or absent

preconditions.condition: The costing method of the product is `fifo` and the product was not handled by the incremental fast path.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other paths applies.

preconditions.condition: The quantity on hand is positive, or a most recent incoming movement exists and yields a non-zero unit price.
preconditions.otherwise: The unit cost is left unchanged.

procedure: Take the product's quantity on hand inside the valued perimeter.
When it is positive, set the unit cost to the total value divided by the quantity on hand.
When it is not positive, find the most recent incoming movement of the product.
When such a movement exists and yields a non-zero unit price, set the unit cost to that unit price.
Otherwise leave the unit cost unchanged.
records.formula: unit_cost = total_value ÷ quantity_on_hand when quantity_on_hand > 0 ; unit_cost = unit_price_of_the_last_incoming_move when the quantity on hand is not positive and that price is non-zero ; unit_cost unchanged otherwise

rounding.precision: None on storage: full floating precision.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: unit cost of the product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the product's unit cost field with automatic revaluation disabled; it is a reporting figure, not a valuation driver.

edge_cases.case: The quantity on hand is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost falls back to the unit price of the last incoming movement, or stays unchanged when there is none.

edge_cases.case: The quantity on hand is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The same fallback applies.

edge_cases.case: The last incoming movement has a value of zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Its unit price is zero, so the cost is left unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The product is a kit.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded from the valuation product domain and its computed total value and average cost are forced to zero.

worked_examples.description: A product holding one hundred and sixteen units worth 1 799.00
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand seven hundred and ninety-nine divided by one hundred and sixteen is 15.508620…, stored at full floating precision and displayed as 15.51 at two decimal places.

worked_examples.description: A product with a quantity on hand of minus ten whose last receipt of ten units was valued at 80.00
worked_examples.narrative: The quantity on hand is not positive, so the cost becomes the unit price of the last incoming movement, 80.00 divided by ten, which is 8.00.

records.name: The full path for the unit cost under average cost
records.purpose: Rebuilds the average unit cost by replaying the movements, which is the only way to get the right figure when an outgoing movement was valued in the same completion or when history was edited.

operands.name: set of products using average cost
operands.source: the average cost group that survived the incremental fast path
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: force recomputation flag
operands.source: this path, which always forces the replay
operands.constraints: always on here

preconditions.condition: The costing method of the product is `average` and the product was not handled by the incremental fast path.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other paths applies.

preconditions.condition: The replay produced a figure for the product.
preconditions.otherwise: The product's unit cost is left unchanged.

procedure: Replay the average over the whole set of products with the recomputation forced, so the fast exit of the replay is not taken.
Write the resulting unit cost onto each product for which the replay produced a figure, with the flag that disables automatic revaluation.
records.formula: unit_cost( product ) = the running unit cost the average replay leaves behind for that product

rounding.precision: None on storage: full floating precision.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: unit cost of the product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the product's unit cost field with automatic revaluation disabled.

edge_cases.case: A product has no anchor in the valuation history.
edge_cases.outcome: The replay starts from the beginning of time for the whole batch, because the narrowing is applied only when every product has an anchor.

edge_cases.case: A product has no movement at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The replay produces no figure for it and its unit cost is left unchanged.

edge_cases.case: Stock went negative and then recovered.
edge_cases.outcome: The replay's recovery branch rebuilds the value from the arriving goods, and the resulting unit cost is written.

edge_cases.case: The product is valuated by lot.
edge_cases.outcome: It never reaches this path; its cost is the aggregate of its lots' costs.

worked_examples.description: A product whose history is ten units in at 100.00, twenty units in at 300.00, fifteen out and ten out
worked_examples.narrative: The replay gives a cost of 10.00 after the first receipt, then 400.00 over thirty units, which is 13.333333…; fifteen units leave at that cost, leaving 200.00 over fifteen units; ten more leave, leaving 66.666666… over five units, displayed as 66.67.

records.name: Selecting the last incoming movement of a product
records.purpose: Picks the single most recent receipt of a product, which is the fallback the first in first out path and the first in first out extrapolation use when there is nothing on hand to value against.

operands.name: movements of the product whose incoming flag is set
operands.source: the completed movements of the product
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: as-of instant
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: when given, movements dated after it are excluded

preconditions.condition: At least one movement of the product carries the incoming flag and is dated not after the as-of instant.
preconditions.otherwise: There is no last incoming movement and the caller falls back to the product's unit cost or leaves the cost unchanged.

procedure: Restrict to the movements of the product whose incoming flag is set.
When an as-of instant is given, drop the movements dated after it.
Order the survivors by date and, for equal dates, by identifier.
Keep the movement with the greatest date and identifier.
records.formula: last_incoming_move = the movement with the greatest ( date , identifier ) among the movements of the product whose incoming flag is set and whose date is not after the as-of instant, when one is given

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the selection itself.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the last incoming movement
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the first in first out path and by the first in first out extrapolation.

edge_cases.case: Two receipts share the same date.
edge_cases.outcome: The one with the higher identifier wins, because ties are broken by identifier descending.

edge_cases.case: No receipt exists at all.
edge_cases.outcome: There is no last incoming movement; the caller leaves the unit cost unchanged or uses the product's unit cost.

edge_cases.case: An as-of instant is given.
edge_cases.outcome: Receipts after that instant are invisible, so a past valuation is not disturbed by a later receipt.

worked_examples.description: Three receipts on days one, three and six, valued as of day five

inputs.as_of_instant: the last instant of day five

worked_examples.narrative: The receipt of day six is dated after the as-of instant and is dropped; the greatest remaining date is day three.

records.name: Unit price of a selection of movements
records.purpose: Turns a set of movements into one price per unit by dividing their total value by their total valued quantity, which is how the last incoming movement yields a fallback cost.

operands.name: total value of the selection
operands.source: the sum of the value fields of the movements selected
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: total valued quantity of the selection
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the sum of the valued quantities of the movements selected
operands.constraints: may be zero

preconditions.condition: The total valued quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The unit price is zero.

procedure: Sum the values of the movements in the selection.
Sum their valued quantities.
Divide the total value by the total valued quantity, or report zero when that quantity is zero.
records.formula: unit_price = total_value_of_the_selection ÷ total_valued_quantity_of_the_selection ; unit_price = 0 when the total valued quantity is zero

rounding.precision: None on the intermediate figure; the Product Price decimal precision on display.
rounding.method: Half away from zero on display.
rounding.step: At display time only.

result.name: unit price of the selection
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed as a fallback unit cost and as the base of the first in first out extrapolation.

edge_cases.case: The selection is a single movement.
edge_cases.outcome: The rule reduces to the movement's value divided by its valued quantity.

edge_cases.case: The total valued quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit price is zero, whatever value the movements carry.

edge_cases.case: The total value is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit price is negative.

worked_examples.description: One receipt of ten units valued at 80.00
worked_examples.narrative: Eighty divided by ten is 8.00.

worked_examples.description: A selection whose total valued quantity is zero
worked_examples.narrative: The total valued quantity is zero, so the rule reports zero rather than dividing.

records.name: The standard price batch valuation
records.purpose: Produces the unit cost and the total value of each product using standard price, reading the cost from the valuation history when the caller asks for a past instant.

operands.name: unit cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product, when no as-of instant is given
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: value of the latest valuation history record not after the as-of instant
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the valuation history of the product, when an as-of instant is given
operands.constraints: absent when the product has no such record

operands.name: quantity on hand
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: already scoped by the caller to the valued perimeter, the company and the as-of instant when given
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

preconditions.condition: The costing method of the product is `standard`.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two batch routines applies.

preconditions.condition: When an as-of instant is given, a valuation history record exists for the product not after that instant.
preconditions.otherwise: The product's current unit cost is used instead.

procedure: When no as-of instant is given, take the product's current unit cost.
When an as-of instant is given, take the value of the latest valuation history record of that product not after the instant, falling back to the product's current unit cost when there is none.
Multiply the quantity on hand, already scoped by the caller, by the chosen unit cost to obtain the total value.
records.formula: unit_cost( product ) = product_unit_cost when no as-of instant ; unit_cost( product ) = value_of_the_latest_valuation_history_record for that product not after the as-of instant, falling back to product_unit_cost when there is none ; total_value( product ) = quantity_on_hand( product ) × unit_cost( product )

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: When the total value is displayed or written; the unit cost keeps full floating precision.

result.name: unit cost and total value of each product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit, and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the inventory valuation report and consumed by the closing computation.

edge_cases.case: The valuation history of the product was deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: The past valuation falls back to the product's current cost.

edge_cases.case: The quantity on hand is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The total value is negative, exactly the quantity multiplied by the cost.

edge_cases.case: A cost change is dated exactly at the as-of instant.
edge_cases.outcome: It is seen, because the lookup uses date not after the as-of instant.

worked_examples.description: A product whose cost was 10.00 on day one and 12.00 on day five, holding thirty units
worked_examples.narrative: Valued today the cost is the current one, 12.00, and thirty multiplied by 12.00 is 360.00.

worked_examples.description: The same product valued as of day three

inputs.as_of_instant: the last instant of day three

worked_examples.narrative: The latest valuation history record not after day three carries 10.00, and the quantity on hand as of day three multiplied by 10.00 is the total value; with ten units on hand that is 100.00.

records.name: Selecting the latest valuation history record per product
records.purpose: Finds, for each product, the most recent deliberate cost change, which serves as the dated cost under standard price and as the anchor the average replay starts from.

operands.name: set of products
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: as-of instant
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: records dated after it are excluded

operands.name: lot
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: when absent, only records with an empty lot are kept

preconditions.condition: The records considered have an empty movement reference.
preconditions.otherwise: A record attached to a movement is a manual correction of that movement, not a cost change, and is excluded.

preconditions.condition: The records belong to the company in the current scope.
preconditions.otherwise: Records of another company are excluded.

procedure: Restrict to the valuation history records of those products whose movement reference is empty, so that only cost changes and never movement corrections are considered, and whose company is the company in the current scope.
When a lot was given, restrict to records whose lot is that lot or whose lot is empty; when no lot was given, restrict to records whose lot is empty.
When an as-of instant was given, restrict to records whose date is not after it.
Order by product, then by date descending, then by identifier descending.
Keep the first record of each product.
records.formula: anchor( product ) = the first record after ordering by product, date descending, identifier descending, among the records of that product with an empty movement reference, of the company in scope, matching the lot condition and not after the as-of instant

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the selection itself; the value it carries is a unit cost at full floating precision.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the anchor record of each product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit for the value it carries
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed as the dated unit cost under standard price and as the seed of the average replay.

edge_cases.case: Two records share the same date.
edge_cases.outcome: The one with the higher identifier wins, so the most recently created cost change governs.

edge_cases.case: The product has no record at all.
edge_cases.outcome: No anchor exists; under standard price the current cost is used, and the average replay starts from the beginning of time.

edge_cases.case: A record is attached to a movement.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, because its movement reference is not empty; it is a manual correction, not a cost change.

edge_cases.case: A lot was given and a record carries no lot.
edge_cases.outcome: It is kept, because the condition accepts a record whose lot is that lot or whose lot is empty.

worked_examples.description: A product with a cost change on day one at 10.00 and another on day five at 12.00, selected as of day three

inputs.as_of_instant: the last instant of day three

worked_examples.narrative: The record of day five is dated after the as-of instant and is dropped, so the first record after ordering is the one of day one carrying 10.00.

records.name: The average replay: fast exit
records.purpose: Returns the stored average figures without replaying anything when no as-of instant and no forced recomputation were asked for, which is what keeps ordinary reads cheap.

operands.name: unit cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: quantity on hand
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the product, in the valued perimeter of the company in scope
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

preconditions.condition: No as-of instant was given and the force recomputation flag is off.
preconditions.otherwise: The replay runs in full.

procedure: Return the product's current unit cost as the unit cost.
Return the quantity on hand multiplied by that unit cost as the total value.
Do not fetch or replay any movement.
records.formula: unit_cost = product_unit_cost ; total_value = quantity_on_hand × product_unit_cost

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: When the total value is displayed.

result.name: unit cost and total value of each product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit, and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the inventory valuation report and consumed by the closing computation.

edge_cases.case: The quantity on hand is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The total value is negative, exactly the quantity multiplied by the cost.

edge_cases.case: An as-of instant is given.
edge_cases.outcome: The fast exit is not taken and the replay runs.

edge_cases.case: The force recomputation flag is on.
edge_cases.outcome: The fast exit is not taken; this is the path the full average unit cost recomputation uses.

worked_examples.description: A product holding twenty units at a stored average cost of 12.50
worked_examples.narrative: No replay happens; twenty multiplied by 12.50 is 250.00.

records.name: Seeding the average replay from the latest manual cost change
records.purpose: Sets the starting state of the replay from each product's anchor, so that the replay can begin at the last deliberate cost change instead of at the beginning of time.

operands.name: value of the anchor record
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the latest valuation history record of the product with an empty movement reference
operands.constraints: absent when the product has no anchor

operands.name: quantity at the anchor's date
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the quantity of the lot when a lot is given, otherwise of the product, as it stood at the anchor's date
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: oldest anchor date
operands.source: the earliest anchor date across the products of the set
operands.constraints: used only when every product of the set has an anchor

preconditions.condition: The product has an anchor.
preconditions.otherwise: No seeding happens for it; its running state starts empty and the first movement of the product supplies it.

preconditions.condition: Every product of the set has an anchor.
preconditions.otherwise: The movement filter is not narrowed, because a product without an anchor must be replayed from the beginning of time.

procedure: Find the latest manual cost change of each product of the set.
Let the oldest anchor be the earliest date among them, and add the condition date not before the oldest anchor to the movement filter only when every product of the set has an anchor.
For each product that has an anchor, set the running unit cost to the anchor's value.
Set the running quantity to the quantity of the lot when a lot is given, otherwise of the product, as it stood at the anchor's date.
Set the running value to the anchor's value multiplied by that quantity.
Remember the anchor's date as that product's replay start.
records.formula: running_unit_cost = anchor_value ; running_quantity = quantity at the anchor's date ; running_value = anchor_value × running_quantity ; replay_start = anchor_date

rounding.precision: None on the running state, which keeps full floating precision.
rounding.step: Not applicable; only the reported total value is rounded, at display.

result.name: the running state of each anchored product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency and the reference unit of measure
result.stored_or_displayed: Held in memory for the duration of the replay; not stored.

edge_cases.case: One product of the batch has no anchor.
edge_cases.outcome: The filter is not narrowed for the whole batch, so one anchorless product disables the optimisation rather than producing a wrong figure for it.

edge_cases.case: The anchor's date is later than some movements.
edge_cases.outcome: Those movements are dropped, because a movement dated not after the replay start is considered already reflected in the anchor.

edge_cases.case: The valuation history of a product was deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: It loses its anchor and replays from the beginning of time.

edge_cases.case: The quantity at the anchor's date is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The running value starts at zero whatever the anchor's value.

worked_examples.description: A product anchored on day four at 12.00 while holding twenty units on that day
worked_examples.narrative: The running value is 12.00 multiplied by twenty, which is 240.00, and the replay starts just after day four.

records.name: The average replay: the incoming branch in the ordinary case
records.purpose: Folds an arriving quantity and its value into the running average when stock was already positive, which is the weighted average of the domain.

operands.name: valued quantity of the movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the incoming movement being replayed
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: value of the movement
operands.source: the incoming movement being replayed
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: running quantity before the movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the replay state of that product
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero in this branch

operands.name: running value before the movement
operands.source: the replay state of that product
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: valued quantity of the movement for the lot
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the movement, when a lot filter is active
operands.constraints: used to scale the entering value

preconditions.condition: The movement carries the incoming flag.
preconditions.otherwise: The outgoing branch applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The previous running quantity is strictly greater than zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The recovery branch applies instead.

procedure: Take the entering quantity as the movement's valued quantity and the entering value as the movement's value.

When a lot filter is active, scale the entering value by the lot quantity divided by the entering quantity, taking zero when the entering quantity is zero, and replace the entering quantity by the lot quantity.
Remember the previous quantity and add the entering quantity to the running quantity.
Add the entering value to the running value.
Set the running unit cost to the running value divided by the running quantity.
records.formula: entering_quantity = movement_valued_quantity ; entering_value = movement_value ; previous_quantity = quantity ; quantity = quantity + entering_quantity ; value = value + entering_value ; unit_cost = value ÷ quantity

rounding.what: The running value and the running unit cost.
rounding.precision: None on the running state, which keeps full floating precision; the decimal places of the company currency on the reported total value.
rounding.method: Half away from zero on the reported figure.
rounding.step: Only when the total value is reported; never during the replay.

result.name: running quantity, running value and running unit cost
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held in memory during the replay; the final unit cost is written on the product and the final value is reported as the total value.

edge_cases.case: A lot filter is active and the entering quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The entering value is scaled to zero.

edge_cases.case: The movement is both incoming and outgoing.
edge_cases.outcome: The incoming branch runs first and the outgoing branch then uses the updated unit cost.

edge_cases.case: The entering value is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The running quantity grows while the running value does not, so the unit cost falls.

edge_cases.case: The previous quantity is zero or negative.
edge_cases.outcome: This branch does not apply; the recovery branch does.

worked_examples.description: Ten units on hand worth 100.00 receiving twenty more valued at 300.00
worked_examples.narrative: The previous quantity of ten is greater than zero, so the values add: 100.00 plus 300.00 is 400.00 over thirty units, giving a unit cost of 13.333333….

worked_examples.description: Ten units on hand worth 100.00 receiving ten more valued at 150.00
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred plus one hundred and fifty is 250.00 over twenty units, giving 12.50.

records.name: The average replay: the incoming branch recovering from negative stock
records.purpose: Rebuilds the running value from the arriving goods alone when stock was zero or negative, which is how the domain corrects a delivery that was valued before the goods had arrived.

operands.name: entering quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the incoming movement being replayed, restricted to the lot when a lot filter is active
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: entering value
operands.source: the incoming movement being replayed, scaled to the lot when a lot filter is active
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: running quantity before the movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the replay state of that product
operands.constraints: zero or negative in this branch

preconditions.condition: The movement carries the incoming flag.
preconditions.otherwise: The outgoing branch applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The previous running quantity is zero or negative.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary incoming branch applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The entering quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The unit cost is left unchanged and only the value is rebuilt from it.

procedure: Add the entering quantity to the running quantity.
Set the running unit cost to the entering value divided by the entering quantity, leaving it unchanged when the entering quantity is zero.
Set the running value to the running unit cost multiplied by the running quantity, rather than accumulating the entering value.
records.formula: quantity = quantity + entering_quantity ; unit_cost = entering_value ÷ entering_quantity ( unchanged when entering_quantity is 0 ) ; value = unit_cost × quantity

rounding.what: The running value and the running unit cost.
rounding.precision: None on the running state; the decimal places of the company currency on the reported total value.
rounding.method: Half away from zero on the reported figure.
rounding.step: Only when the total value is reported.

result.name: running quantity, running value and running unit cost
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held in memory during the replay; the final unit cost is written on the product.

edge_cases.case: The entering quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit cost is left unchanged and the value is rebuilt from the unchanged cost.

edge_cases.case: The running quantity is still negative after the receipt.
edge_cases.outcome: The value is the unit cost multiplied by a negative quantity, so it stays negative.

edge_cases.case: The previous quantity was exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The branch still applies, so the arriving goods set the cost outright.

edge_cases.case: Several receipts follow one another while stock is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: Each one resets the cost to its own unit price until the quantity turns positive.

worked_examples.description: Delivering five units at a cost of 10.00 from nothing, then receiving ten units valued at 110.00
worked_examples.narrative: The delivery takes the value to minus 50.00 at a quantity of minus five. At the receipt the previous quantity is negative, so the unit cost is taken from the entering movement alone, 110.00 divided by ten, which is 11.00, and the value is rebuilt as 11.00 multiplied by five, which is 55.00 rather than the 60.00 accumulation would give. The 5.00 difference is the correction of the earlier delivery.

records.name: The average replay: the outgoing branch
records.purpose: Takes goods out of the running state at the average as it stands before the movement, leaving the unit cost untouched, which is what makes a delivery cost the average of the day.

operands.name: valued quantity of the movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the outgoing movement being replayed
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: running unit cost before the movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the replay state of that product
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: valued quantity of the movement for the lot
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the movement, when a lot filter is active
operands.constraints: used to scale the leaving value

preconditions.condition: The movement carries the outgoing flag.
preconditions.otherwise: The incoming branch applies instead.

preconditions.condition: A running unit cost exists for the product.
preconditions.otherwise: The unit cost defaults to the movement's value divided by its valued quantity, or zero when that quantity is zero.

procedure: Take the leaving quantity as the movement's valued quantity.
Compute the leaving value as the leaving quantity multiplied by the running unit cost as it stands before the movement.

When a lot filter is active, scale the leaving value by the lot quantity divided by the leaving quantity, taking zero when the leaving quantity is zero, and replace the leaving quantity by the lot quantity.
Subtract the leaving value from the running value and the leaving quantity from the running quantity.
Leave the running unit cost unchanged.
records.formula: leaving_quantity = movement_valued_quantity ; leaving_value = leaving_quantity × unit_cost ; value = value − leaving_value ; quantity = quantity − leaving_quantity ; unit_cost unchanged

rounding.precision: None on the running state; the decimal places of the company currency on the reported total value.
rounding.method: Half away from zero on the reported figure.
rounding.step: Only when the total value is reported.

result.name: running quantity and running value
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held in memory during the replay.

edge_cases.case: The running quantity goes negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The value goes negative with it, at the unchanged unit cost.

edge_cases.case: The movement is both incoming and outgoing.
edge_cases.outcome: The incoming branch has already run, so the outgoing branch uses the updated unit cost.

edge_cases.case: The leaving quantity is zero and a lot filter is active.
edge_cases.outcome: The leaving value is scaled to zero.

edge_cases.case: The product has no running state yet.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit cost defaults to the movement's own value divided by its valued quantity, or zero when that quantity is zero.

worked_examples.description: Fifteen units leaving a running state of thirty units worth 400.00 at 13.333333…
worked_examples.narrative: Fifteen multiplied by 13.333333… is 200.00, so the value falls from 400.00 to 200.00 and the quantity from thirty to fifteen, while the unit cost stays 13.333333….

worked_examples.description: Ten more units leaving the same state
worked_examples.narrative: Ten multiplied by 13.333333… is 133.333333…, leaving 66.666666… over five units, reported as 66.67 after currency rounding.

records.name: The average replay: the ordered walk over the movements
records.purpose: Rebuilds the weighted average of every product of a set from its movements, which is the only figure the domain trusts when the average must be recomputed or read as of a past instant.

operands.name: set of products
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: as-of instant
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: adds the condition date not after it to the movement filter

operands.name: lot
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: adds the condition has a line carrying that lot

operands.name: force recomputation flag
operands.source: the caller
operands.constraints: when off and no as-of instant is given, the fast exit is taken

operands.name: movements of the products
operands.source: the movements of those products in the company in scope that are incoming or outgoing
operands.constraints: ordered by product, then date, then identifier

preconditions.condition: An as-of instant was given or the force recomputation flag is on.
preconditions.otherwise: The fast exit returns the stored figures and no replay happens.

preconditions.condition: The movements are walked in the order product, date, identifier.
preconditions.otherwise: Two movements at the same instant would be replayed in an arbitrary order and the average would not be reproducible.

procedure: Take the fast exit when there is no as-of instant and the force flag is off.

Build the movement filter: movements of the products in the set, of the company in the current scope, that are incoming or outgoing; add the lot condition when a lot is given and the date condition when an as-of instant is given.
Find the latest manual cost change per product and, when every product of the set has one, add the condition date not before the oldest anchor to the filter.
Seed the running state of each anchored product from its anchor.
Fetch the movements ordered by product, then date, then identifier, and drop every movement whose date is not after its product's replay start.
Replay the surviving movements in order, applying the incoming branch, the recovery branch or the outgoing branch as each movement requires.
Return the running unit cost and the running value of each product.
records.formula: for each movement in order: apply the incoming branch when the movement is incoming, then the outgoing branch when it is outgoing ; the result is the running unit cost and the running value of each product

rounding.what: The reported total value of each product.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency for the reported value; the running state is kept at full floating precision.
rounding.step: Only when the total value is reported or written; never between movements.

result.name: unit cost and total value of each product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit, and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: The unit cost is written on the product with automatic revaluation disabled; the total value is displayed on the inventory valuation report.

edge_cases.case: A movement is dated exactly at the anchor instant.
edge_cases.outcome: It is dropped, because it is considered already reflected in the anchor.

edge_cases.case: One product of the set has no anchor.
edge_cases.outcome: The filter is not narrowed for the whole set, so every product is replayed from the beginning of time.

edge_cases.case: A movement is both incoming and outgoing.
edge_cases.outcome: The incoming branch runs first and the outgoing branch then uses the updated unit cost.

edge_cases.case: A product has no running state when its first movement is replayed.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit cost defaults to that movement's value divided by its valued quantity, or zero when that quantity is zero.

edge_cases.case: The history is very long.
edge_cases.outcome: The movements are fetched in pages; a conforming rebuild need not reproduce the page size but must produce the same results for arbitrarily large histories.

worked_examples.description: A product whose whole history is ten units in at 100.00, twenty units in at 300.00, fifteen out and ten out
worked_examples.narrative: Ten in at 100.00 gives a cost of 10.00 over ten units. Twenty in at 300.00 with a previous quantity of ten gives a value of 400.00 over thirty units and a cost of 13.333333…. Fifteen out at that cost leaves 200.00 over fifteen units. Ten out leaves 66.666666… over five units, reported as 66.67.

records.name: The first in first out batch valuation
records.purpose: Produces the total value and the unit cost of each product using first in first out, by valuing the quantity on hand against the stack of receipts that still hold it.

operands.name: quantity on hand
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the product's quantity in the valued perimeter, or the lot quantity when a lot is given
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: lot
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: restricts both the quantity and the stack

operands.name: as-of instant
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: restricts the stack to movements not after it

operands.name: location
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: scopes the quantity computation and flips the stack to outgoing movements when the location is outside the valued perimeter

preconditions.condition: The costing method of the product is `fifo`.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two batch routines applies.

preconditions.condition: The quantity on hand is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The unit cost is reported as zero.

procedure: Take the quantity on hand of the product, or the lot quantity when a lot is given.
Value that quantity under first in first out, with the lot, the as-of instant and the location the caller supplied.
Divide the resulting total value by the quantity to obtain the unit cost, reporting zero when the quantity is zero.
records.formula: quantity = quantity_on_hand( product ) , or the lot quantity when a lot is given ; total_value = fifo_value( product , quantity , lot , as_of_instant , location ) ; unit_cost = total_value ÷ quantity , or 0 when quantity is 0

rounding.what: The total value and the unit cost.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency for the total value; the unit cost keeps full floating precision.
rounding.step: When the total value is reported or written.

result.name: unit cost and total value of each product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit, and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the inventory valuation report and consumed by the closing computation.

edge_cases.case: The quantity on hand is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The total value is zero and the unit cost is reported as zero.

edge_cases.case: The quantity on hand is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The non-positive branch of the first in first out valuation applies and the total value is the quantity multiplied by the reference cost, which is negative.

edge_cases.case: More is asked for than the company ever received.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder is extrapolated from the last movement used or from the product's unit cost.

edge_cases.case: The product is a kit.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded from the valuation product domain and its computed total value and average cost are forced to zero.

records.name: Building the first in first out stack
records.purpose: Produces the ordered list of receipts that are considered still to hold the quantity on hand, oldest first, together with the part of the oldest one that is still on hand, which is the structure every first in first out figure is read from.

operands.name: quantity on hand
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the lot's quantity when a lot is given, otherwise the product's quantity on hand scoped to the valued perimeter and to the as-of instant
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: quantity already processed in this call
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the context threaded through a batch of outgoing movements
operands.constraints: zero when absent

operands.name: completed incoming movements of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: a collection of movements with their valued quantities
operands.source: the movements of the product, of any company in the current scope, matching the lot, date and location conditions
operands.constraints: fetched newest first in pages of one hundred

operands.name: location
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: when it is outside the valued perimeter, the outgoing flag is required instead of the incoming flag

preconditions.condition: The stack size, after the quantity already processed has been subtracted, is greater than zero at the precision of the unit of measure.
preconditions.otherwise: An empty stack and a bottom quantity of zero are returned.

preconditions.condition: The movements are fetched ordered by date descending and identifier descending.
preconditions.otherwise: The stack would not reflect the receipts that actually hold the quantity on hand.

procedure: When a location was given, scope the quantity computation to that location and remember whether that location is outside the valued perimeter.
Set the stack size to the lot's quantity when a lot was given, otherwise to the product's quantity on hand scoped to the valued perimeter and to the as-of instant.
Subtract the quantity already processed in this call from the stack size, when the context carries one.
Return an empty stack and a bottom quantity of zero when the stack size is not greater than zero at the precision of the unit of measure.

Build the movement filter: movements of this product, of any company in the current scope, with the lot condition when a lot was given, the date condition when an as-of instant was given, and the destination-location condition when a location was given; then require the outgoing flag when that location is outside the valued perimeter and the incoming flag otherwise.
Fetch the movements ordered by date descending and identifier descending, in pages of one hundred.

Walk them newest first, appending each movement to the stack, setting the bottom quantity to the smaller of that movement's valued quantity and the stack size as it stands, then subtracting the valued quantity from the stack size.
Stop when the stack size is no longer greater than zero or when the movements run out, fetching the next page while the stack size is still positive.
Reverse the stack so that the oldest movement is first and return it together with the bottom quantity.
records.formula: stack_size = quantity_on_hand − quantity_already_processed ; for each movement newest first: bottom_quantity = min( movement_valued_quantity , stack_size ) ; stack_size = stack_size − movement_valued_quantity ; stop when stack_size ≤ 0

rounding.what: The stack size and the bottom quantity, for the comparison only.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the unit of measure, 0.01 by default.
rounding.method: Half away from zero on the comparison.
rounding.step: At the test that decides whether the stack size is still greater than zero.

result.name: the stack, oldest first, and the bottom quantity
result.unit_or_currency: a list of movements, and the reference unit of measure of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the first in first out valuation and by the remaining quantity computation.

edge_cases.case: The quantity on hand is not positive.
edge_cases.outcome: The stack is empty and the bottom quantity is zero, so the caller extrapolates.

edge_cases.case: The receipts are exhausted before the stack size is covered.
edge_cases.outcome: The stack holds every receipt and the caller extrapolates the uncovered remainder.

edge_cases.case: Two receipts share the same date.
edge_cases.outcome: They are consumed in identifier order, oldest identifier first, because the stack is built newest first by date and identifier and then reversed.

edge_cases.case: A receipt's quantity was increased after the fact.
edge_cases.outcome: The added units enter at the top of the queue, because the stack is rebuilt from the current quantity on hand and not from a consumption ledger.

edge_cases.case: The location given is outside the valued perimeter.
edge_cases.outcome: The filter requires the outgoing flag instead of the incoming flag, so goods that left towards that location form the stack.

edge_cases.case: The stack search spans several companies.
edge_cases.outcome: It covers every company in the current scope, unlike the average replay, which is restricted to the single company in scope.

records.name: Valuing a quantity under first in first out
records.purpose: Produces the money value of a given quantity of a product by consuming the stack of receipts from the oldest, which is the figure a delivery is valued at and the figure the total value of a product reports.

operands.name: quantity to value
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the caller: the valued quantity of an outgoing movement, or the quantity on hand of the product
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative, which takes the non-positive branch

operands.name: stack of receipts
operands.unit_or_currency: a list of movements with their values and valued quantities
operands.source: the first in first out stack building rule
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: bottom quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the first in first out stack building rule
operands.constraints: the part of the oldest movement of the stack that is still on hand

operands.name: lot
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: restricts the offered quantity and scales the offered value

operands.name: unit cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product, used for the extrapolation when no movement was used
operands.constraints: may be zero

preconditions.condition: The quantity to value is greater than zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The non-positive branch applies and the value is the quantity multiplied by the reference cost.

preconditions.condition: The stack is not empty, or the extrapolation can fall back to the product's unit cost.
preconditions.otherwise: The value is zero.

procedure: Take the non-positive branch when the quantity to value is not greater than zero.
Build the stack and set the accumulated cost to zero.
While the quantity still to value is greater than zero and the stack is not empty, pop the oldest movement and remember it as the last movement used.

For the first iteration, when a bottom quantity was returned, offer the bottom quantity and the proportional part of the movement's value, then clear the bottom quantity so this branch is not taken again.

Otherwise offer the movement's valued quantity, restricted to the lot when a lot was given, and the movement's value, scaled by the lot quantity divided by the valued quantity when a lot was given and taking zero when that quantity is zero.

When the offered quantity exceeds the quantity still to value, scale the offered value by the quantity still to value divided by the offered quantity and reduce the offered quantity to the quantity still to value.
Add the offered value to the accumulated cost and subtract the offered quantity from the quantity still to value.
Extrapolate the remainder when the stack is exhausted and a quantity still remains.
Return the accumulated cost.
records.formula: fifo_value = Σ over the movements popped, oldest first, of the value each offers , with the offered value scaled by ( quantity_still_to_value ÷ offered_quantity ) on the last movement, plus the extrapolation of any remainder

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: When the accumulated cost is written on a movement or reported as a total value; the per-layer proportions are not rounded.

result.name: first in first out value of the quantity
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the movement's value field when the caller is the valuation routine, or reported as the total value of the product.

edge_cases.case: The quantity to value is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The non-positive branch returns zero.

edge_cases.case: The quantity to value exceeds everything ever received.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder is extrapolated from the last movement used, or from the product's unit cost when no movement was used.

edge_cases.case: A receipt's quantity was increased after the fact.
edge_cases.outcome: The stack is rebuilt from the current quantity on hand, so the added units are considered still on hand at the top of the queue.

edge_cases.case: A lot is given and a movement's valued quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The offered value is scaled to zero.

edge_cases.case: The movement offering the last units offers more than is needed.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the proportional part of its value is taken and the rest stays on the stack for a later call.

records.purpose: Values a quantity that is zero or negative without touching the stack, at the product's or the lot's cost, or at the unit price of the last receipt when a past instant is asked for.

operands.name: quantity to value

operands.constraints: zero or negative in this branch

operands.name: unit cost of the lot

operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: unit cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product, when no lot was given

preconditions.condition: The quantity to value is not greater than zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary stack-consuming branch applies.

procedure: Let the reference cost be the lot's cost when a lot was given, otherwise the product's unit cost.
When an as-of instant was given, look up the last incoming movement not after that instant and, when one exists, use its unit price instead of the reference cost.
Multiply the quantity by the chosen cost and return the product.

records.purpose: Takes only the part of the oldest receipt that is still on hand, at that receipt's own unit price, which is what keeps a partly consumed receipt from being counted twice.

operands.name: bottom quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the stack building rule
operands.constraints: not greater than the movement's valued quantity

preconditions.condition: This is the first iteration of the consumption loop and a bottom quantity was returned.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary branch applies and the whole valued quantity of the movement is offered.

records.purpose: Values the part of a quantity that no receipt can cover, which happens when more is asked for than the company ever received, so that a delivery against negative stock still carries a cost.

operands.name: remaining quantity after the stack is exhausted
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the consumption loop
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero in this branch

operands.name: value of the last movement used
operands.source: the last movement popped from the stack
operands.constraints: absent when the stack was empty

operands.name: valued quantity of the last movement used
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the same movement

operands.name: unit cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: may be zero

preconditions.condition: A quantity still remains after the stack is exhausted.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is extrapolated.

preconditions.condition: A last movement was used and its valued quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The product's unit cost is used instead of that movement's unit price.

Otherwise take the product's unit cost.
Multiply the remaining quantity by the chosen price and add the result to the accumulated cost.

records.purpose: Distributes the quantity on hand back onto the receipts that are considered to still hold it, so that a reader can see which receipt is still in stock and so that a landed cost knows how much of a receipt is left to revalue.

operands.constraints: may be empty

For each lot, or for the single pass, build the stack and skip when it is empty.
Assign the bottom quantity to the first movement of the stack.
Assign the full valued quantity to every subsequent movement of the stack, accumulating per movement across lots.
Report the resulting map from product to movement to quantity.

preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two branches applies.

preconditions.condition: The product carries a unit cost.
preconditions.otherwise: The movement is valued at zero and the goods leave at no cost.

procedure: Value the movement at the product's unit cost multiplied by its valued quantity, exactly as for a movement made against positive stock.
Let the quantity on hand and the total value both go negative.

operands.constraints: may be empty

preconditions.otherwise: The split is refused with the message "You cannot apply landed costs on the chosen _the target label_(s). Landed costs can only be applied for products with first in first out or average costing method.", where the target label is "Transfers" or "Manufacturing Orders".

preconditions.condition: The product's costing method is `fifo` or `average`.
preconditions.otherwise: The movement is skipped, because a standard-price product's cost is an input that a landed cost must not move.

procedure: Take the movements of the selected transfers.
Add, when manufacturing landed costs are installed, the finished-goods movements of the selected manufacturing orders, minus the by-product movements whose cost share is zero.
Replace, when subcontracting landed costs are installed, every targeted movement that is a subcontracting movement by its originating movements.

records.name: The landed cost split computation
records.purpose: Spreads each cost line of a landed cost document across the goods movements it targets, and attaches the rounding residue so that the allocated amounts add up to the cost exactly.

operands.name: cost lines of the document
operands.source: the document
operands.constraints: at least one, otherwise nothing is split

operands.name: valuation lines
operands.unit_or_currency: a collection of lines with a quantity, a former cost, a weight and a volume
operands.source: the valuation line collection rule
operands.constraints: at least one, otherwise the document is skipped

operands.name: rounding step of the company currency
operands.source: the company's currency record
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero

operands.name: split method of each cost line
operands.unit_or_currency: one of the five stored values `by_quantity`, `by_weight`, `by_volume`, `equal` and `by_current_cost_price`
operands.source: the cost line
operands.constraints: one of the five

preconditions.condition: The document has at least one targeted movement.
preconditions.otherwise: The document is skipped and no adjustment line is created for it.

preconditions.condition: The totals are summed once per valuation line and not once per created adjustment line.
preconditions.otherwise: Adding a second cost line would double the totals and every share would be halved.

procedure: Delete every existing valuation adjustment line of the documents being computed.
Take each document that has at least one targeted movement in turn, with the document's company in scope, and let the rounding be the rounding step of the company currency.
Collect the valuation lines and create, for each of them, one adjustment line per cost line of the document.

Accumulate, once per valuation line and not once per created adjustment line, the total quantity, the total weight, the total volume, the total cost as the sum of the former costs each rounded to the currency, and the number of valuation lines.
Take each cost line in turn, set the running split total to zero, and compute the raw share of each of its adjustment lines by the split method of that cost line.
Round each raw share to the currency, half away from zero, add it to the split total and accumulate it onto its adjustment line.

After the cost line is fully split, compute the residue as the cost amount minus the split total, rounded to the currency, and add it to the adjustment line with the highest identifier among all adjustment lines accumulated so far when it is not zero for the currency.
Write the accumulated amounts onto the adjustment lines.
records.formula: total_quantity = Σ line_quantity ; total_weight = Σ line_weight ; total_volume = Σ line_volume ; total_cost = Σ round_to_currency( line_former_cost ) ; total_lines = the number of valuation lines ; each raw share is rounded to the currency and accumulated ; residue = round_to_currency( cost_amount − split_total )

rounding.what: Each raw share, and the residue.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Each share immediately after it is computed and before it is added to the split total; the residue after the cost line is fully split.

result.name: the additional landed cost of each adjustment line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the adjustment line and consumed by the extra source of the priority chain and by the landed cost journal entry.

edge_cases.case: The document has several cost lines.
edge_cases.outcome: Each valuation line receives one adjustment line per cost line, and the totals are still summed once per valuation line.

edge_cases.case: The residue of an earlier cost line is not zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It lands on the adjustment line with the currently highest identifier, which with several cost lines means the residues all pile onto the same line.

edge_cases.case: A cost amount is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The split is handled identically and the residue is computed the same way; the shares are negative.

edge_cases.case: The split method's condition fails, for example a total weight of zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The share falls back to the cost amount divided by the number of valuation lines.

edge_cases.case: An adjustment line already exists on the document.
edge_cases.outcome: Every existing adjustment line is deleted before the computation starts.
