edge_cases.case: One line carries a former cost of zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It takes a share of zero and the whole cost lands on the others.

edge_cases.case: A former cost is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: Its share is negative while the others are positive, and the split total still reaches the cost amount through the residue.

worked_examples.description: One hundred split by value across goods worth 300.00 and goods worth 100.00
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred divided by a total cost of 400.00 is 0.25 per unit of value, so the first line takes 300.00 multiplied by 0.25, which is 75.00, and the second 100.00 multiplied by 0.25, which is 25.00.

records.name: Landed cost share when the split method's condition fails
records.purpose: Falls back to an equal split whenever the divisor a split method needs is zero, so that a cost is always fully allocated even when the goods carry no weight, no volume or no value.

operands.name: amount of the cost line
operands.source: the cost line of the document
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: number of valuation lines
operands.source: the valuation line collection
operands.constraints: at least one

operands.name: divisor the chosen method needs
operands.unit_or_currency: a quantity, a weight, a volume or the company currency
operands.source: the total quantity, total weight, total volume or total cost of the valuation lines
operands.constraints: zero in this situation, which is what triggers the fallback

preconditions.condition: The split method of the cost line is one of `by_quantity`, `by_weight`, `by_volume` or `by_current_cost_price` and its divisor is zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The method's own formula applies.

preconditions.condition: At least one valuation line exists.
preconditions.otherwise: The document is skipped and nothing is split.

procedure: Detect that the total the chosen method divides by is zero.
Compute the raw share as the cost amount divided by the number of valuation lines instead.
Round it to the currency and add it to the split total, exactly as for an equal split.
records.formula: raw_share = cost_amount ÷ total_lines , whenever the chosen method's total is zero

rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Immediately after the raw share is computed.

result.name: share of the cost line allocated to the movement
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Accumulated onto the adjustment line's additional landed cost.

edge_cases.case: The split method is `by_weight` and no product carries a weight.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost is split equally over the valuation lines.

edge_cases.case: The split method is `by_volume` and no product carries a volume.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost is split equally.

edge_cases.case: The split method is `by_current_cost_price` and every former cost is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost is split equally.

edge_cases.case: The split method is `by_quantity` and the total quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost is split equally, although a movement with a quantity of zero is skipped when the valuation lines are collected.

worked_examples.description: Sixty split by weight across two movements of products that carry no weight
worked_examples.narrative: The total weight is zero, so the condition fails and the share becomes 60.00 divided by two, which is 30.00 for each line; the split total reaches 60.00 exactly.

records.name: The rounding residue of a landed cost split
records.purpose: Gives the last hundredths that rounding lost to one adjustment line, so that the amounts allocated from a cost line add up to that cost line exactly.

operands.name: amount of the cost line
operands.source: the cost line of the document
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: split total
operands.source: the sum of the rounded shares of that cost line
operands.constraints: accumulated as each share is rounded

operands.name: identifiers of the adjustment lines accumulated so far
operands.source: the whole computation, across every cost line processed so far
operands.constraints: the highest identifier receives the residue

preconditions.condition: The cost line has been fully split.
preconditions.otherwise: The residue cannot be computed yet.

preconditions.condition: The residue is not zero for the currency.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is added and the shares stand as rounded.

procedure: Subtract the split total from the cost amount.
Round the difference to the currency.
When it is not zero for the currency, add it to the adjustment line with the highest identifier among all adjustment lines accumulated so far in the whole computation.
records.formula: residue = round_to_currency( cost_amount − split_total )

rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: After the cost line is fully split, before the accumulated amounts are written.

result.name: residue added to one adjustment line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Added to the additional landed cost of the adjustment line with the highest identifier.

edge_cases.case: The residue is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is added and the shares stand as rounded.

edge_cases.case: The document has several cost lines.
edge_cases.outcome: The residues of the earlier cost lines all land on the same currently highest adjustment line, so the per-cost-line sum check can fail even though the overall check passes; the recomputation is offered explicitly for that reason.

edge_cases.case: The cost amount is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The residue is computed the same way and may be negative.

edge_cases.case: The residue is attached to a line of a different cost line.
edge_cases.outcome: That is the specified behaviour: the residue goes to the highest identifier, not to the largest line and not to the last line of the same cost line.

worked_examples.description: One hundred split equally over three movements

expected_outputs.line_receiving_the_residue: the adjustment line with the highest identifier

worked_examples.narrative: One hundred minus 99.99 is 0.01, which is not zero for the currency, so it is added to the adjustment line with the highest identifier, taking it from 33.33 to 33.34.

worked_examples.description: One hundred split by quantity across thirty and twenty units
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred minus one hundred is zero, which is zero for the currency, so nothing is corrected.

records.name: The landed cost sum check
records.purpose: Refuses to validate a landed cost whose allocated amounts no longer add up to its costs, which is the guard against a stale split after the costs or the targets were edited.

operands.name: additional landed cost of each adjustment line
operands.source: the adjustment lines of the document
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: total amount of the document
operands.source: the document
operands.constraints: the sum of its cost lines

operands.name: amount of each cost line
operands.source: the cost lines of the document
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

preconditions.condition: The document is in the `draft` state.
preconditions.otherwise: The validation is refused with the message "Only draft landed costs can be validated".

preconditions.condition: The document has at least one targeted movement.
preconditions.otherwise: The validation is refused with the message "Please define _the target label_ on which those additional costs should apply."

procedure: Sum the additional landed costs over all the adjustment lines of the document and compare the sum with the document total; the absolute difference must be zero for the currency.

For every cost line that has at least one adjustment line, sum the additional landed costs over that cost line's adjustment lines and compare the sum with the cost line's amount; the absolute difference must be zero for the currency.
Refuse the validation when either comparison fails.
records.formula: | Σ additional_landed_cost over all adjustment lines − amount_total | is zero for the currency , and , for every cost line that has at least one adjustment line , | cost_line_amount − Σ additional_landed_cost over that cost line's adjustment lines | is zero for the currency

rounding.what: Both differences, for the comparison only.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, inherited from the currency rounding of the zero test.
rounding.step: At the moment of the comparison, before the document may be validated.

result.name: acceptance or refusal of the validation
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it gates the transition of the document to the posted state.

edge_cases.case: Either comparison fails.
edge_cases.outcome: The validation is refused with the message "Cost and adjustments lines do not match. You should maybe recompute the landed costs."

edge_cases.case: A cost line has no adjustment line at all.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not checked individually; only cost lines with at least one adjustment line are.

edge_cases.case: The residues of several cost lines piled onto one adjustment line.
edge_cases.outcome: The overall check still passes but the per-cost-line check can fail, which is why the recomputation is offered explicitly.

edge_cases.case: A document in the posted state is cancelled or deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: The system refuses with the message "Validated landed costs cannot be cancelled, but you could create negative landed costs to reverse them".

worked_examples.description: A document of one hundred split into 33.33, 33.33 and 33.34
worked_examples.narrative: The allocated amounts sum to exactly 100.00, so both differences are zero for the currency and the document may be validated.

worked_examples.description: The same document after a cost line was raised to 120.00 without recomputing
worked_examples.narrative: The allocated amounts still sum to 100.00 while the total is 120.00, so the difference of 20.00 is not zero for the currency and the validation is refused with the message about costs and adjustment lines not matching.

records.name: Source six of the priority chain: landed costs
records.purpose: Adds the posted landed costs of a movement on top of the value the other sources produced, without claiming any quantity, so that freight and duty raise the cost of the goods they were incurred for.

operands.name: additional landed cost of each adjustment line attached to this movement
operands.source: the adjustment lines whose document is in the posted state
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: state of the landed cost document
operands.source: the document each adjustment line belongs to
operands.constraints: only documents in the posted state contribute

operands.name: as-of instant
operands.source: the caller, optionally
operands.constraints: restricts to documents whose date is not after it

preconditions.condition: The flag add extra is still on, that is no manual correction claimed the quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: The source is not consulted at all, because a human who adjusts a movement's value is stating the final value, landed costs included.

preconditions.condition: At least one adjustment line attached to this movement belongs to a posted document.
preconditions.otherwise: The source contributes nothing.

procedure: Collect the adjustment lines attached to this movement whose document is in the posted state, restricting to documents whose date is not after the as-of instant when one is given.
Contribute nothing when there are none.
Otherwise add the sum of their additional landed costs to the value, claiming no quantity.

Build the justification, one line per adjustment line, as "+ _the formatted amount_ from _the vendor bill display name_ (Landed Cost: _the document display name_)" when the document has a vendor bill and "+ _the formatted amount_ (Landed Cost: _the document display name_)" otherwise, joined by newlines under the heading "Additional landed costs:".
records.formula: extra_value = Σ additional_landed_cost over the adjustment lines of this movement whose document is posted and whose date is not after the as-of instant ; claimed_quantity = 0

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency; each additional landed cost was already rounded when the split was written.
rounding.step: When the accumulated movement value is written.

result.name: contribution of the extra source
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Accumulated into the movement's value on top of the other sources, without claiming quantity.

edge_cases.case: A manual correction claimed the quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The source is suppressed, so the landed costs are not counted twice; the human's figure is the final value.

edge_cases.case: The document is still in the draft state.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not contribute; only posted documents reach the value.

edge_cases.case: An as-of instant is given and the document is dated after it.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not contribute, so a past valuation is not disturbed by a later landed cost.

edge_cases.case: The additional landed cost is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The value is reduced by that amount.

edge_cases.case: Several posted documents target the same movement.
edge_cases.outcome: Their amounts are summed and each contributes one justification line.

worked_examples.description: A receipt of ten units worth 100.00 from the product cost, with a posted landed cost of 20.00
worked_examples.narrative: The extra source adds the 20.00 of the posted adjustment line without claiming any quantity, so the movement's value rises from 100.00 to 120.00.

worked_examples.description: The same receipt where a human adjusted the value to 150.00
worked_examples.narrative: The manual correction turned the flag add extra off, so the source is not consulted and the 20.00 is not added; the ledger and the physical value then diverge by 20.00 until the next closing absorbs it.

records.name: The amount a landed cost posts to the ledger
records.purpose: Posts only the share of a landed cost that relates to goods still in stock, because the cost of the goods that have already left was recognised at the price that was known when they left.

operands.name: additional landed cost of the adjustment line
operands.source: the adjustment line, after the split
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: remaining quantity of the movement at validation time
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the remaining quantity map
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: quantity of the adjustment line
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the valuation line the adjustment line was built from
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero, because zero-quantity movements are skipped

preconditions.condition: The movement's product has the `real_time` valuation mode.
preconditions.otherwise: No journal items are produced for that line; under periodic valuation the closing carries the effect instead.

preconditions.condition: The remaining quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No journal items are produced for that line, because the goods have already left and there is nothing left in stock to revalue.

procedure: Read the movement's remaining quantity at validation time.
Multiply the additional landed cost by the remaining quantity divided by the line quantity.
Produce no journal items for the line when the remaining quantity is zero.
Debit the inventory valuation account and credit the cost line's counterpart account by the resulting amount, swapping the two sides when the amount is negative.
records.formula: posted_amount = additional_landed_cost × ( remaining_quantity ÷ line_quantity )

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: When the journal item is written.

result.name: amount posted for the adjustment line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written as a pair of journal items on the landed cost entry; the full additional landed cost nevertheless enters the movement's value through the extra source.

edge_cases.case: The remaining quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: No journal items are produced for that line; the goods have already left, so there is nothing left in stock to revalue.

edge_cases.case: The remaining quantity is negative, because goods were delivered that were never in stock.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is negative and the two journal items swap sides.

edge_cases.case: The remaining quantity equals the line quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole additional landed cost is posted.

edge_cases.case: The product uses periodic valuation.
edge_cases.outcome: No landed cost entry is produced; the difference surfaces in the next closing as a variation.

edge_cases.case: The cost line has no counterpart account and the cost product has no expense account.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry is refused with the message "Please configure Stock Expense Account for product: _the cost product name_."

worked_examples.description: Sixty allocated to a receipt of thirty units of which eighteen are still on hand
worked_examples.narrative: Sixty multiplied by eighteen divided by thirty is 36.00, which is debited to the inventory valuation account and credited to the cost line's counterpart account. The full 60.00 nevertheless enters the movement's value through the extra source, so the remaining value of the movement rises by the proportional share.

worked_examples.description: Forty allocated to a receipt of twenty units of which none are still on hand
worked_examples.narrative: Nought divided by twenty is zero, so the posted amount is zero and no journal items are produced for that line.

worked_examples.description: Minus fifty allocated to a receipt of twenty units all still on hand
worked_examples.narrative: Minus fifty multiplied by twenty divided by twenty is minus 50.00, so the two journal items swap sides: the counterpart account is debited 50.00 and the inventory valuation account credited 50.00.

records.name: The total cost of a manufacturing order
records.purpose: Adds up everything a manufacturing order consumed, so that the finished goods and the by-products can be priced from one figure.

operands.name: value of each consumed component movement
operands.source: the component movements of the order, as the valuation engine valued them
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: work-centre cost
operands.source: the sum over the work orders of the order
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: extra unit cost of the order
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the order
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: quantity of the finished movements
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the finished product
operands.source: the sum over the finished movements of the movement quantity converted into the product reference unit
operands.constraints: strictly positive, because movements with a non-positive quantity are excluded

preconditions.condition: At least one finished-goods movement of the order for the order's own product has a state that is neither completed nor cancelled and a positive quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: The computation stops and no price is written.

preconditions.condition: The component movements have been valued.
preconditions.otherwise: Their values are whatever the valuation engine wrote, which may be zero.

procedure: Take the finished movements: the finished-goods movements of the order for the order's own product whose state is neither completed nor cancelled and whose quantity is positive.
Stop when there are none.
Sum the work-centre cost over the order's work orders.
Let the quantity be the sum, over the finished movements, of the movement quantity converted into the product reference unit.
Multiply the order's extra unit cost by that quantity to obtain the extra cost.
Add the values of the consumed component movements, the work-centre cost and the extra cost to obtain the total cost.
records.formula: extra_cost = order_extra_unit_cost × quantity ; total_cost = Σ value of the consumed component movements + work_centre_cost + extra_cost

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency.
rounding.step: When the resulting unit prices are written onto the movements; the total cost itself is kept unrounded through the division.

result.name: total cost of the manufacturing order
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored on its own; divided into the unit prices of the finished-goods and by-product movements.

edge_cases.case: The order has no work order.
edge_cases.outcome: The work-centre cost is zero.

edge_cases.case: The extra unit cost is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The extra cost is zero.

edge_cases.case: A component movement was valued at zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes nothing and the finished goods are cheaper by that much.

edge_cases.case: Every finished movement is already completed or cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: The computation stops and no price is written.

worked_examples.description: An order producing ten units, consuming three component movements worth 78.00, 180.00 and 20.00, with work orders costing 200.00 and no extra unit cost
worked_examples.narrative: Seventy-eight plus one hundred and eighty plus twenty is 278.00; adding the work-centre cost of 200.00 and an extra cost of zero gives a total cost of 478.00.

records.name: Unit price of a by-product under first in first out or average cost
records.purpose: Gives a by-product its share of the manufacturing cost, so that the finished goods and the by-products together carry exactly the cost of the order.

operands.name: total cost of the order
operands.source: the manufacturing cost computation
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: cost share of the by-product
operands.source: the by-product line of the order
operands.constraints: must be non-zero at two decimals for this branch to apply

operands.name: quantity of the by-product movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the by-product
operands.source: the movement quantity converted into the product reference unit
operands.constraints: must be positive for the division to be meaningful

preconditions.condition: The by-product movement is neither completed nor cancelled and has a positive quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: It is skipped and no price is written for it.

preconditions.condition: The by-product's costing method is `fifo` or `average`.
preconditions.otherwise: The unit price is the by-product's own unit cost, under standard price.

preconditions.condition: The cost share is non-zero at two decimals.
preconditions.otherwise: The by-product keeps its existing unit price and is skipped, but its cost share of zero is still accumulated.

procedure: Convert the by-product movement's quantity into the by-product's reference unit.
Multiply the total cost by the cost share and divide by one hundred to obtain the by-product's share of the cost.
Divide that share by the by-product quantity to obtain the unit price, reporting zero when the quantity is zero.
Accumulate the cost share into the total by-product cost share, whether or not a price was written.
records.formula: by_product_quantity = convert( by_product_move_quantity → product_reference_unit ) ; by_product_unit_price = total_cost × cost_share ÷ 100 ÷ by_product_quantity ( 0 when the quantity is zero )

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency for the value it produces; the cost share is compared at two decimals.
rounding.step: When the movement's value is written; the unit price itself is kept unrounded.

result.name: unit price of the by-product movement
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the by-product
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the by-product movement's unit price field and consumed by the production source of the priority chain.

edge_cases.case: The cost share rounds to zero at two decimals.
edge_cases.outcome: The by-product keeps its existing unit price and is skipped, but its cost share of zero is still accumulated.

edge_cases.case: The by-product quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit price is zero.

edge_cases.case: The by-product uses standard price.
edge_cases.outcome: Its own unit cost is used instead of the share.

edge_cases.case: The by-product movement is already completed or cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not priced at all.

edge_cases.case: The by-product carries a cost share of zero and a landed cost targets the order.
edge_cases.outcome: The by-product movement is removed from the landed cost targets.

worked_examples.description: A by-product carrying a cost share of twenty-five percent, five units, from an order whose total cost is 478.00
worked_examples.narrative: Four hundred and seventy-eight multiplied by twenty-five and divided by one hundred is 119.50; divided by five units that is 23.90 per unit.

records.name: Unit price of a by-product under standard price
records.purpose: Leaves a by-product using standard price at its own input cost, so that the manufacturing cost does not move a cost the operator set deliberately.

operands.name: unit cost of the by-product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the by-product, as the operator set it
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: cost share of the by-product
operands.source: the by-product line of the order
operands.constraints: still accumulated into the total by-product cost share

preconditions.condition: The by-product movement is neither completed nor cancelled and has a positive quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: It is skipped and no price is written for it.

preconditions.condition: The by-product's costing method is `standard`.
preconditions.otherwise: The share branch applies instead.

procedure: Read the by-product's own unit cost.
Write it as the unit price of the by-product movement.
Accumulate the by-product's cost share into the total by-product cost share, which still reduces the finished goods' share.
records.formula: by_product_unit_price = by_product_unit_cost , when the costing method is standard price

rounding.precision: None on the unit cost, which keeps full floating precision; the decimal places of the company currency on the movement value it produces.
rounding.method: Half away from zero on the movement value.
rounding.step: When the movement's value is written.

result.name: unit price of the by-product movement
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the by-product
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the by-product movement's unit price field.

edge_cases.case: The by-product's unit cost is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The by-product movement is valued at zero, while its cost share still reduces the finished goods' share.

edge_cases.case: The cost share is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The finished goods take the whole cost and the by-product still takes its own standard cost.

edge_cases.case: The cost share is large and the standard cost is small.
edge_cases.outcome: The two figures are independent: the finished goods lose the share while the by-product takes only its standard cost, so the order's cost is not fully redistributed.

worked_examples.description: A by-product using standard price with a unit cost of 20.00, five units, from an order whose total cost is 478.00 and whose by-product share is twenty-five percent
worked_examples.narrative: The by-product takes its own standard cost of 20.00 per unit, so its movement is worth 100.00, while the accumulated share of twenty-five percent still reduces the finished goods' share of the 478.00.

records.name: Unit price of the finished goods under standard price
records.purpose: Leaves a finished product using standard price at its own input cost, so that a manufacturing order does not move a standard cost.

operands.name: unit cost of the finished product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product, as the operator set it
operands.constraints: may be zero

preconditions.condition: At least one finished movement is neither completed nor cancelled and has a positive quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: No price is written.

preconditions.condition: The finished product's costing method is `standard`.
preconditions.otherwise: The share-based branch applies instead.

procedure: Read the finished product's own unit cost.
Write it as the unit price of every finished movement of the order.
records.formula: finished_unit_price = finished_product_unit_cost , when the finished product's costing method is standard price

rounding.precision: None on the unit cost, which keeps full floating precision; the decimal places of the company currency on the movement value it produces.
rounding.method: Half away from zero on the movement value.
rounding.step: When the movement's value is written.

result.name: unit price of the finished movements
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the finished product
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on each finished movement's unit price field and consumed by the production source of the priority chain.

edge_cases.case: The finished product's unit cost is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The finished goods enter stock at no value, whatever the order consumed.

edge_cases.case: The order consumed more than the standard cost.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is not carried into the finished goods; under perpetual valuation it stays on the accounts the component movements credited.

edge_cases.case: A by-product carries a cost share.
edge_cases.outcome: It does not reduce the finished goods' unit price, which is the standard cost.

worked_examples.description: Ten finished units of a standard-price product whose unit cost is 40.00, from an order whose total cost is 478.00
worked_examples.narrative: The finished goods take the standard cost of 40.00 per unit, so the movement is worth 400.00 rather than the 478.00 the order consumed.

records.name: Unit price of the finished goods under first in first out or average cost
records.purpose: Prices the finished goods at the part of the manufacturing cost the by-products did not take, so that the order's whole cost is distributed across everything it produced.

operands.name: total cost of the order
operands.source: the manufacturing cost computation
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: total by-product cost share
operands.source: the sum of the cost shares accumulated over the by-product movements
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: quantity of the finished movements
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the finished product
operands.source: the sum over the finished movements of the movement quantity converted into the product reference unit
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: At least one finished movement is neither completed nor cancelled and has a positive quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: No price is written.

preconditions.condition: The finished product's costing method is not `standard`.
preconditions.otherwise: The product's own unit cost is used instead.

procedure: Compute the complement of the by-product share as one minus the total by-product cost share divided by one hundred.
Round that complement to the nearest multiple of one ten-thousandth, ties away from zero.
Multiply the total cost by the rounded complement.
Divide the result by the quantity of the finished movements to obtain the unit price.
Write it as the unit price of every finished movement of the order.
records.formula: finished_unit_price = total_cost × round_half_up( 1 − total_by_product_cost_share ÷ 100 , 0.0001 ) ÷ quantity

rounding.what: The complement of the by-product cost share.
rounding.precision: One ten-thousandth for the complement; the decimal places of the company currency for the movement value.
rounding.step: The complement immediately before it multiplies the total cost; the movement value when it is written.

result.name: unit price of the finished movements
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the finished product
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on each finished movement's unit price field and consumed by the production source of the priority chain.

edge_cases.case: There is no by-product.
edge_cases.outcome: The total by-product cost share is zero, the complement is 1.0000 and the finished goods take the whole cost.

edge_cases.case: The by-product shares add up to one hundred percent.
edge_cases.outcome: The complement is zero and the finished goods are priced at zero.

edge_cases.case: A by-product whose cost share rounds to zero at two decimals was skipped.
edge_cases.outcome: Its zero share was still accumulated, so the complement is unaffected.

edge_cases.case: The quantity of the finished movements is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: There is no finished movement to price, because movements with a non-positive quantity are excluded.

worked_examples.description: Ten finished units from an order whose total cost is 478.00 with no by-product
worked_examples.narrative: The complement is one minus nought divided by one hundred, which rounds to 1.0000; 478.00 multiplied by 1.0000 and divided by ten is 47.80, so the finished-goods movement values at ten multiplied by 47.80, which is 478.00.

worked_examples.description: The same order also producing a by-product carrying twenty-five percent in a quantity of five
worked_examples.narrative: The complement is one minus twenty-five divided by one hundred, which rounds to 0.7500; 478.00 multiplied by 0.7500 and divided by ten is 35.85, so the finished goods take 358.50 and the by-product takes 119.50; together 478.00.

records.name: The unit price of a kit
records.purpose: Recombines the unit prices of the components of a kit into one price per kit, because a kit has no movement of its own to read a price from.

operands.name: exploded component quantities
operands.unit_or_currency: the component reference units of measure
operands.source: the explosion of the kit bill of materials for the valued quantity
operands.constraints: one entry per component

operands.name: unit price of the movements of each component
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per component reference unit
operands.source: the drop-shipment unit price when any of the component's movements is a drop shipment, otherwise the ordinary unit price
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: kit quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the kit
operands.source: the quantity the explosion was run for
operands.constraints: must be non-zero for the ratio to be meaningful

operands.name: valued quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the kit
operands.source: the movement set being priced
operands.constraints: may be zero

preconditions.condition: The product is built from a kit bill of materials.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary unit price of the movements applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The valued quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The kit price unit is zero.

procedure: Explode the kit for the valued quantity, obtaining the quantity required of each component.
Accumulate, per component, the quantity per kit as the sum of the exploded line quantities converted into the component reference unit.
Take, for each component, the unit price of the movements of that component: the drop-shipment unit price when any of them is a drop shipment, otherwise the ordinary unit price.
Sum, over the components, the component unit price multiplied by the component quantity per kit divided by the kit quantity, to obtain the total price unit.
Divide the total price unit by the valued quantity, reporting zero when that quantity is zero.
records.formula: component_quantity_per_kit = Σ convert( exploded_line_quantity → component_reference_unit ) ; total_price_unit = Σ over components of component_unit_price × ( component_quantity_per_kit ÷ kit_quantity ) ; kit_price_unit = total_price_unit ÷ valued_quantity ( 0 when the valued quantity is zero )

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency on the value it produces; the price itself is kept unrounded.
rounding.step: When the value of the movement is written.

result.name: unit price of the kit
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the kit
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed as the cost ratio of the quotation source of the priority chain and by the cost-of-goods-sold computation.

edge_cases.case: The valued quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The kit price unit is zero.

edge_cases.case: A component has no movement.
edge_cases.outcome: Its unit price is zero and the kit is priced without it.

edge_cases.case: A component's movements include a drop shipment.
edge_cases.outcome: The drop-shipment unit price is used for that component, which re-evaluates each movement through the priority chain rather than reading the stored field.

edge_cases.case: The kit itself is a valuation product.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not: a kit product is excluded from the valuation product domain and its computed total value and average cost are forced to zero, so its components are not counted twice.

worked_examples.description: A kit of one unit made of two components, two units of one costing 5.00 and three of another costing 2.00
worked_examples.narrative: The first component contributes 5.00 multiplied by two divided by one, which is 10.00, and the second 2.00 multiplied by three divided by one, which is 6.00; the total price unit is 16.00 and, divided by a valued quantity of one, the kit price unit is 16.00.

records.name: Cost of a product computed from its bill of materials
records.purpose: Builds the cost of a manufactured product from its operations and its components, recursing into child bills of materials, which is what the action that computes a price from a bill of materials writes onto the product.

operands.name: cost of each operation of the bill of materials
operands.source: the operations not skipped for this product
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: quantity of each component line
operands.source: the component lines not skipped for this product
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: unit cost of each component
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per component reference unit
operands.source: the component product, or the recursive cost of its child bill of materials when that child is itself scheduled for recomputation
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: total by-product cost share
operands.source: the sum of the cost shares of the by-products of the bill of materials
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: quantity of the bill of materials
operands.source: the bill of materials
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero

preconditions.condition: The bill of materials has at least one operation or one component line that is not skipped for this product.
preconditions.otherwise: The total is zero and the computed cost is zero.

preconditions.condition: The bill quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The division cannot be performed.

procedure: Start the total at zero and add the cost of every operation of the bill of materials that is not skipped for this product.

For every component line that is not skipped for this product, when the line has a child bill of materials that is itself scheduled for recomputation, compute that child's cost recursively, convert it from the child product's reference unit into the line unit, and multiply by the line quantity.
Otherwise convert the component's unit cost from the component reference unit into the line unit and multiply by the line quantity.
When at least one by-product carries a cost share, multiply the total by the complement of the summed shares, rounded to the nearest multiple of one ten-thousandth.
Divide the total by the bill quantity and convert the resulting price from the bill unit of measure into the product reference unit.
records.formula: total = Σ operation costs + Σ over the component lines of line_quantity × the component cost converted into the line unit ; total = total × round_half_up( 1 − Σ by_product_cost_share ÷ 100 , 0.0001 ) when at least one by-product carries a cost share ; result = convert_price( total ÷ bill_quantity , bill_unit_of_measure → product_reference_unit )

rounding.what: The complement of the by-product shares, and the resulting price.
rounding.precision: One ten-thousandth for the complement; the Product Price decimal precision for the price written on the product.
rounding.step: The complement immediately before it multiplies the total; the price when it is written onto the product.

result.name: cost of the main product of the bill of materials
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Written onto the product's unit cost by the action that computes a price from a bill of materials.

edge_cases.case: A component line has a child bill of materials that is not scheduled for recomputation.
edge_cases.outcome: The component's stored unit cost is used instead of recursing.

edge_cases.case: An operation or a component line is skipped for this product.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes nothing.

edge_cases.case: No by-product carries a cost share.
edge_cases.outcome: The total is not reduced and the whole cost goes to the main product.

edge_cases.case: The bill unit of measure differs from the product reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The price is converted after the division, so the result is per reference unit.

edge_cases.case: A component's unit cost is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes nothing to the total.

worked_examples.description: A bill of materials producing one unit from operations costing 200.00 and components worth 78.00, 180.00 and 20.00, with no by-product
worked_examples.narrative: Two hundred plus seventy-eight plus one hundred and eighty plus twenty is 478.00; there is no by-product share, and dividing by a bill quantity of one leaves 478.00 per unit.

worked_examples.description: The same bill producing ten units with a by-product carrying twenty-five percent
worked_examples.narrative: The total of 478.00 is multiplied by the complement of 0.7500, giving 358.50, and divided by a bill quantity of ten, giving 35.85 per unit.

records.name: Cost of a by-product computed from a bill of materials
records.purpose: Gives a by-product of a bill of materials its share of the computed cost, so that the action that computes prices from bills of materials prices the by-products as well as the main product.

operands.name: total cost of the bill of materials
operands.source: the operations and the components, before the by-product complement is applied
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: by-product share
operands.source: the sum of the cost shares of the by-product's lines
operands.constraints: must be non-zero for a price to be produced

operands.name: by-product quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the by-product
operands.source: the sum of the by-product line quantities converted into the by-product reference unit
operands.constraints: must be non-zero for a price to be produced

preconditions.condition: The by-product carries a non-zero cost share.
preconditions.otherwise: The result is zero.

preconditions.condition: The by-product quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The result is zero.

procedure: Sum the by-product line quantities converted into the by-product reference unit.
Sum the cost shares of those lines.
Multiply the total by the share, divide by one hundred, and divide by the by-product quantity.
Report zero when either the share or the quantity is zero.
records.formula: result = total × by_product_share ÷ 100 ÷ by_product_quantity when both the share and the quantity are non-zero, else 0

rounding.precision: The Product Price decimal precision.
rounding.step: When the price is written onto the by-product.

result.name: cost of the by-product
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the by-product
result.stored_or_displayed: Written onto the by-product's unit cost by the action that computes prices from bills of materials.

edge_cases.case: The by-product share is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero.

edge_cases.case: The by-product quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero.

edge_cases.case: Several lines of the bill of materials produce the same by-product.
edge_cases.outcome: Their quantities and their shares are summed before the division.

worked_examples.description: A by-product carrying twenty-five percent of a total of 478.00 in a quantity of five
worked_examples.narrative: Four hundred and seventy-eight multiplied by twenty-five and divided by one hundred is 119.50; divided by five that is 23.90 per unit.

worked_examples.description: A by-product carrying a share of zero
worked_examples.narrative: The share is zero, so the rule reports zero rather than dividing.

records.name: Cost of goods sold unit price of a set of movements
records.purpose: Turns the movements reachable from an invoice line into one cost per unit, with deliveries counting positive and returns negative, so that the cost recognised follows the goods that actually left.

operands.name: valued quantity of each movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the movements of the set, all of the same product
operands.constraints: counted negative for an incoming movement and positive otherwise

operands.name: value of each movement
operands.source: the movements of the set
operands.constraints: counted negative for an incoming movement and positive otherwise

operands.name: quantity of each consigned valued line
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the consigned lines of those movements, converted into the reference unit
operands.constraints: counted negative when the destination is inside the valued perimeter and positive otherwise

operands.name: unit cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product, used as the fallback
operands.constraints: may be zero

preconditions.condition: Every movement of the set belongs to the same product.
preconditions.otherwise: The result is zero.

preconditions.condition: The total valued quantity is not zero, and either the costing method is `fifo` or `average` or the consigned quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The product's unit cost is used as the unit price.

procedure: Sum the valued quantities of the movements, counting an incoming movement negative and every other movement positive, to obtain the signed quantity.

Sum the quantities of the consigned valued lines of those movements, counting a line whose destination is inside the valued perimeter negative and every other line positive, to obtain the consigned quantity.
Add the two to obtain the total valued quantity.
Sum the values of the movements with the same sign convention to obtain the signed value.
Divide the signed value by the total valued quantity when that quantity is not zero and either the costing method is `fifo` or `average` or the consigned quantity is not zero.
Otherwise take the product's unit cost.
Report zero when the set contains movements of more than one product.
records.formula: signed_quantity = Σ over the movements of valued_quantity × ( −1 when the movement is incoming , +1 otherwise ) ; consigned_quantity = Σ over the consigned valued lines of line_quantity_in_reference_unit × ( −1 when the destination is inside the valued perimeter , +1 otherwise ) ; total_valued_quantity = signed_quantity + consigned_quantity ; signed_value = Σ over the movements of move_value × ( −1 when the movement is incoming , +1 otherwise ) ; unit_price = signed_value ÷ total_valued_quantity when total_valued_quantity ≠ 0 and ( the costing method is fifo or average , or consigned_quantity ≠ 0 ) ; unit_price = product_unit_cost otherwise

rounding.precision: None on the unit price itself; the decimal places of the company currency on the amount it produces.
rounding.step: When the amount of the cost-of-goods-sold item is written.

result.name: cost of goods sold unit price of the set
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the cost-of-goods-sold value of an invoice line.

edge_cases.case: The set contains movements of more than one product.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero.

edge_cases.case: A delivery of ten is followed by a return of three.
edge_cases.outcome: The net quantity is seven and the net value is the cost of seven units, because the return counts negative.

edge_cases.case: The total valued quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The product's unit cost is used.

edge_cases.case: The product uses standard price and there is no consigned quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The product's unit cost is used, not the value that left.

edge_cases.case: A consigned line crosses the perimeter.
edge_cases.outcome: It is added to the denominator with its own sign, so that a consignment flow does not distort the unit cost, even though a consigned line never enters a valued quantity.

worked_examples.description: Two deliveries of a product using first in first out, six units worth 60.00 and four units worth 48.00
worked_examples.narrative: The signed quantity is six plus four, which is ten, and the signed value is 60.00 plus 48.00, which is 108.00; the unit price is 108.00 divided by ten, which is 10.80.

worked_examples.description: A delivery of ten worth 100.00 followed by a return of three worth 30.00
worked_examples.narrative: The return counts negative, so the signed quantity is ten minus three, which is seven, and the signed value is 100.00 minus 30.00, which is 70.00; the unit price is 10.00.

records.name: Cost of goods sold value of an invoice line
records.purpose: Produces the unit price of the cost-of-goods-sold items injected on a customer invoice, recognising exactly the cumulative cost of the goods sold minus what earlier documents already recognised.

operands.name: unit price of the movements reachable from the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the cost-of-goods-sold unit price of the completed movements reachable from the line, or a fallback when there are none
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: cost-of-goods-sold quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the cost-of-goods-sold quantity rule
operands.constraints: signed; negative for a customer credit note

operands.name: already-posted cost-of-goods-sold value
operands.source: the already-posted cost-of-goods-sold value rule
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: line quantity in the reference unit
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the line quantity converted from the line unit of measure
operands.constraints: must be non-zero for the division to be meaningful

preconditions.condition: The line carries a product and its quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The line's own unit price is returned unchanged.

preconditions.condition: The line is eligible for stock accounting and the company uses the anglo-saxon convention with perpetual valuation.
preconditions.otherwise: No cost-of-goods-sold item is injected at all.

procedure: Take the shortcut first for a product using standard price or average cost, returning the unit price of the matching cost-of-goods-sold line of the original document when one is found.
Return the line's own unit price when there is no product or the line quantity is zero.
Compute the cost-of-goods-sold quantity.
Find the completed goods movements reachable from the line and take their cost-of-goods-sold unit price; when there are none, take the fallback of the product's costing method.
Convert the line quantity from the line unit of measure into the product reference unit.
Multiply the unit price by the cost-of-goods-sold quantity, subtract the already-posted cost-of-goods-sold value, take the absolute value, and divide by the line quantity in the reference unit.
records.formula: cogs_unit_price = | unit_price × cogs_quantity − already_posted_cogs_value | ÷ line_quantity_in_reference_unit

rounding.what: The unit price of the injected items.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency for the amounts; the Product Price decimal precision for the test that decides whether the item is worth creating.
rounding.step: When the amounts of the two injected items are written; the item is skipped when the computed amount is zero in the document currency or the computed unit price is zero at the Product Price precision.

result.name: cost of goods sold unit price of the invoice line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the injected items, which carry the display type `cogs`, together with the line's unit of measure, quantity and analytic distribution.

edge_cases.case: The absolute value is taken.
edge_cases.outcome: The convention of the injected lines already carries the sign, so the sign is supplied by the sign rule of the items and not by this figure.

edge_cases.case: The document is a credit note that reverses an invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: The shortcut returns the unit price recognised on the original document, so the credit note reverses the cost that was recognised rather than recomputing it at today's cost.

edge_cases.case: Nothing has been delivered yet.
edge_cases.outcome: The fallback of the costing method supplies the unit price and the cost is recognised at the invoice.

edge_cases.case: A partial credit note was issued earlier.
edge_cases.outcome: The already-recognised quantity and value are computed over every customer invoice and credit note of the sales orders concerned, so the next invoice recognises the difference.

edge_cases.case: The line has no label.
edge_cases.outcome: The injected items take the empty string; a missing label does not prevent posting.

worked_examples.description: Invoicing six delivered units of a sales order for ten, the delivery being worth 60.00
worked_examples.narrative: Ten multiplied by six is 60.00, minus nothing already posted is 60.00, divided by six is a unit price of 10.00, so the invoice carries a debit of 60.00 to the expense account and a credit of 60.00 to the inventory valuation account.

worked_examples.description: Invoicing the remaining four units after a second delivery worth 48.00
worked_examples.narrative: The unit price over both deliveries is 108.00 divided by ten, which is 10.80. Ten multiplied by 10.80 is 108.00, minus the 60.00 already posted is 48.00, divided by four is 12.00 per unit, so the second invoice recognises exactly the 48.00 that was not yet recognised and the total cost recognised is 108.00, exactly the value that left stock.

records.name: The cost of goods sold shortcut for standard price and average cost
records.purpose: Makes a credit note reverse the cost that was recognised rather than recompute it at today's cost, by reading the unit price back from the original document.

operands.name: cost-of-goods-sold lines of the reversed document
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the lines of the document this one reverses whose display type is `cogs`
operands.constraints: matched on product and unit of measure, with a unit price that is not negative

operands.name: cost-of-goods-sold lines of the customer invoices of the same sales order lines
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: those invoices, when the line belongs to a credit note that is not a reversal
operands.constraints: matched the same way

preconditions.condition: The product's costing method is `standard` or `average`.
preconditions.otherwise: The shortcut does not apply and the ordinary computation runs.

preconditions.condition: At least one matching cost-of-goods-sold line is found.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary computation runs.

procedure: Collect the lines of the reversed document whose display type is `cogs`, whose product and unit of measure match this line, and whose unit price is not negative.
Add, when the line belongs to a credit note that is not a reversal, the cost-of-goods-sold lines of the customer invoices of the same sales order lines, matched the same way.
Return the unit price of the first of them when any is found.
Fall through to the ordinary computation when none is found.
records.formula: cogs_unit_price = the unit price of the first matching cost-of-goods-sold line of the original document

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded by the shortcut; the unit price is reused exactly as it was written.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency, as they were applied to the original item.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, inherited from the original item.
rounding.step: Not applicable; no new rounding occurs.

result.name: cost of goods sold unit price of the credit-note line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the injected items of the credit note.

edge_cases.case: The original invoice carried several lines of the same product and unit of measure.
edge_cases.outcome: The first one's unit price is used for all of them.

edge_cases.case: A matching line has a negative unit price.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded from the match.

edge_cases.case: The product uses first in first out.
edge_cases.outcome: The shortcut does not apply and the cost is recomputed from the movements.

edge_cases.case: The credit note is not a reversal.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost-of-goods-sold lines of the customer invoices of the same sales order lines are considered as well.

worked_examples.description: A credit note reversing an invoice that recognised 10.00 per unit for an average-cost product
worked_examples.narrative: The shortcut finds the original item at 10.00 per unit and reuses it, so the credit note reverses 60.00 and not the 75.00 today's cost of 12.50 would give.

records.name: Cost of goods sold unit price with no completed movement under standard price or average cost
records.purpose: Supplies the unit price when an invoice is issued before anything has been delivered and the product uses standard price or average cost, which is the product's current unit cost.

operands.name: unit cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: completed goods movements reachable from the line
operands.source: the line
operands.constraints: empty in this situation

preconditions.condition: No completed goods movement is reachable from the invoice line.
preconditions.otherwise: The cost-of-goods-sold unit price of the movements is used instead.

preconditions.condition: The product's costing method is `standard` or `average`.
preconditions.otherwise: The first in first out fallback applies.

procedure: Observe that no completed goods movement is reachable from the line.
Take the product's current unit cost as the unit price.
Carry it into the cost-of-goods-sold value computation.
records.formula: unit_price = product_unit_cost , when no completed movement is reachable and the costing method is standard price or average cost

rounding.precision: None on the unit cost; the decimal places of the company currency on the amounts it produces.
rounding.step: When the amounts of the injected items are written.

result.name: cost of goods sold unit price
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the cost-of-goods-sold value of the invoice line.

edge_cases.case: The product's unit cost is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit price is zero, the computed amount is zero and no item is injected.

edge_cases.case: Goods are delivered after the invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: The cost was already recognised at the invoice; the later delivery does not recognise it again, because the already-posted value is subtracted.

edge_cases.case: The product uses first in first out.
edge_cases.outcome: The first in first out fallback applies instead.

worked_examples.description: Invoicing ten units of an average-cost product whose unit cost is 12.50 before anything is delivered
worked_examples.narrative: With no completed movement, the product's unit cost of 12.50 is the unit price; ten multiplied by 12.50 minus nothing already posted, divided by ten, is 12.50 per unit and an amount of 125.00.

records.name: Cost of goods sold unit price with no completed movement under first in first out
records.purpose: Supplies the unit price when an invoice is issued before anything has been delivered and the product uses first in first out, by valuing the quantity to be sold against the current stack.

operands.name: cost-of-goods-sold quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the cost-of-goods-sold quantity rule
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: first in first out value of that quantity
operands.source: the first in first out valuation of the product for that quantity
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: completed goods movements reachable from the line
operands.source: the line
operands.constraints: empty in this situation

preconditions.condition: No completed goods movement is reachable from the invoice line.
preconditions.otherwise: The cost-of-goods-sold unit price of the movements is used instead.

preconditions.condition: The cost-of-goods-sold quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The unit price is zero.

procedure: Observe that no completed goods movement is reachable from the line.
Value the cost-of-goods-sold quantity under first in first out against the current stack.
Divide that value by the cost-of-goods-sold quantity, reporting zero when the quantity is zero.
records.formula: unit_price = fifo_value( cogs_quantity ) ÷ cogs_quantity , or 0 when the cost-of-goods-sold quantity is zero

rounding.precision: The decimal places of the company currency on the amounts it produces.
rounding.step: When the amounts of the injected items are written.

result.name: cost of goods sold unit price
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Consumed by the cost-of-goods-sold value of the invoice line.

edge_cases.case: The cost-of-goods-sold quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit price is zero.

edge_cases.case: The stack cannot cover the quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The first in first out valuation extrapolates the remainder from the last movement used or from the product's unit cost.

edge_cases.case: Nothing is on hand at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole quantity is extrapolated at the product's unit cost.

worked_examples.description: Invoicing ten units before delivery while ten units are held at 10.00 each
worked_examples.narrative: The first in first out value of ten units is 100.00, so the unit price is 10.00. The cost is recognised at the invoice even though nothing has shipped: the inventory valuation account is credited and the expense account debited by 100.00.

records.name: The cost-of-goods-sold quantity of an invoice line
records.purpose: Computes the cumulative quantity for which cost must have been recognised on the sales order lines concerned, so that each invoice recognises the difference rather than starting afresh.

operands.name: line quantity
operands.source: the invoice or credit-note line, converted into the product reference unit
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: document type
operands.unit_or_currency: a customer invoice or a customer credit note
operands.source: the document
operands.constraints: a credit note flips the sign

operands.name: quantities of the already-posted cost-of-goods-sold lines
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the posted lines that hit the product's inventory valuation account and whose origin line belongs to the same sales order lines
operands.constraints: each converted into the product reference unit and signed by its own document type

preconditions.condition: The line carries a product.
preconditions.otherwise: The cost-of-goods-sold quantity is not computed; the line's own unit price is returned instead.

preconditions.condition: The sales integration is installed.
preconditions.otherwise: Only the line's own quantity counts and no already-posted quantity is added.

procedure: Convert the line quantity from the line unit of measure into the product reference unit.
Negate it when the document is a customer credit note, and keep it positive otherwise, to obtain the own quantity.

Add the posted quantity to the own quantity.
records.formula: own_quantity = convert( line_quantity → product_reference_unit ) × ( −1 when the document is a customer credit note , +1 otherwise ) ; posted_quantity = Σ over the already-posted cost-of-goods-sold lines that hit the product's inventory valuation account and whose origin line belongs to the same sales order lines , of convert( posted_line_quantity → product_reference_unit ) × ( −1 when that document is a customer credit note , +1 otherwise ) ; cogs_quantity = posted_quantity + own_quantity

records.name: The price difference of a vendor bill line
records.purpose: Measures how far the price billed by the vendor is from the standard cost the goods entered stock at, which is the amount that must leave the inventory asset.

operands.name: gross unit price of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency per line unit of measure
operands.source: the line's unit price net of discount
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: comparison price
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency per line unit of measure
operands.source: the comparison price rule
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: quantity of the line
operands.source: the bill line
operands.constraints: used as the relevant quantity, without conversion

preconditions.condition: The mechanism runs at all, that is the document is a vendor bill, vendor credit note or vendor receipt, the company uses anglo-saxon accounting, the line is eligible for stock accounting and the product's costing method is `standard`.
preconditions.otherwise: No difference is computed and nothing is posted.

preconditions.condition: A price difference account can be selected, being the category's price difference account mapped through the document's fiscal position.
preconditions.otherwise: The line is skipped and nothing is posted.

procedure: Subtract the comparison price from the gross unit price to obtain the unit difference.
Take the relevant quantity as the line quantity, in the line unit of measure.
Multiply the relevant quantity by the unit difference to obtain the subtotal difference.
records.formula: price_unit_difference = gross_unit_price − valuation_unit_price ; relevant_quantity = line_quantity ; price_subtotal_difference = relevant_quantity × price_unit_difference

rounding.what: The subtotal difference, for the posting test.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the document currency for the zero test, and the Product Price decimal precision for the unit price agreement test.
rounding.step: At the two tests that decide whether the difference is posted, and again when the two journal items are written in the company currency.

result.name: price difference of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the document currency, per unit and in total
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored on its own; it becomes the amount of the two injected journal items.

edge_cases.case: The billed price equals the standard cost.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero, the subtotal difference is zero for the document currency and nothing is posted.

edge_cases.case: The billed price is below the standard cost.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is negative and the two items swap sides, crediting the price difference account.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison price was negated, so the difference has the mirror sign.

edge_cases.case: The line carries a discount.
edge_cases.outcome: The gross unit price is net of the discount, but the unit price agreement test then fails and the difference is not posted.

worked_examples.description: Ten units billed at 10.00 each against a standard cost of 9.00
worked_examples.narrative: Ten minus nine is a unit difference of 1.00; ten units give a subtotal difference of 10.00, which is not zero, so a difference is posted.

records.name: When a price difference is posted
records.purpose: States the two numeric tests and the four structural conditions that decide whether the price difference items are injected, so that a rounding artefact or a discounted line does not produce a spurious entry.

operands.name: subtotal difference
operands.source: the price difference rule
operands.constraints: tested against zero for the document currency

operands.name: raw stored unit price of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency per line unit of measure
operands.source: the line as stored
operands.constraints: compared with the computed unit price

operands.name: computed unit price of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency per line unit of measure
operands.source: the line as computed
operands.constraints: compared with the raw stored unit price

operands.name: Product Price decimal precision
operands.source: the named decimal precision record for product prices
operands.constraints: two by default

preconditions.condition: The document is a vendor bill, a vendor credit note or a vendor receipt, the company uses anglo-saxon accounting, the line is eligible for stock accounting, and the product's costing method is `standard`.
preconditions.otherwise: The mechanism does not run at all and nothing is posted.

preconditions.condition: A price difference account can be selected, being the category's price difference account mapped through the document's fiscal position.
preconditions.otherwise: The line is skipped and nothing is posted.

procedure: Test that the subtotal difference is not zero for the document currency.
Test that the line's raw stored unit price and its computed unit price agree at the Product Price decimal precision.
Post the two journal items only when both tests pass and the four structural conditions hold.
records.formula: post the difference when is_zero_for_currency( price_subtotal_difference ) is false and round( raw_stored_unit_price , Product Price precision ) = round( computed_unit_price , Product Price precision )

rounding.what: Both tested quantities, for the tests only.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the document currency for the zero test; the Product Price decimal precision for the agreement test.
rounding.step: At the moment of each test, before any item is created.

result.name: the decision to post or to skip
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it gates the injection of the two journal items.

edge_cases.case: A discount has been applied to the line.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit price can no longer be rounded for comparison, the agreement test fails and the difference is not posted.

edge_cases.case: The subtotal difference rounds to zero in the document currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is posted.

edge_cases.case: The price difference account is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The line is skipped, even though the difference is not zero.

edge_cases.case: The product does not use standard price.
edge_cases.outcome: The mechanism does not run; under first in first out and average cost the receipt itself carries the billed price.

edge_cases.case: The company does not use the anglo-saxon convention.
edge_cases.outcome: The mechanism does not run.

records.name: The two amounts of a price difference
records.purpose: Moves the difference between the billed price and the standard cost out of the inventory asset and into the price difference account, as a balanced pair of items on the bill itself.

operands.name: relevant quantity
operands.source: the line quantity
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: unit difference
operands.unit_or_currency: the document currency per line unit of measure
operands.source: the price difference rule
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: document currency and company currency
operands.source: the document and the company
operands.constraints: may be the same

operands.name: rate of today's date
operands.unit_or_currency: a ratio of document currency to company currency
operands.source: the currency rates, at today's date
operands.constraints: strictly greater than zero

preconditions.condition: Both numeric tests and the four structural conditions of the posting rule hold.
preconditions.otherwise: No item is produced.

preconditions.condition: A price difference account is selectable through the document's fiscal position.
preconditions.otherwise: The line is skipped.

Multiply the relevant quantity by the negated unit difference and convert it the same way, to obtain the balance of the item on the account the bill line itself used, which under perpetual valuation is the inventory valuation account.
Give both items the line's analytic distribution, no taxes, the display type `cogs` and the relevant quantity.

rounding.step: After the conversion into the company currency, when each journal item is written.

result.name: the two price difference journal items
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Injected on the vendor bill itself, so that posting them never unbalances the document.

edge_cases.outcome: The two balances swap their signs, so the price difference account is credited and the inventory valuation account debited.

edge_cases.case: The document currency is the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion leaves the amounts unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The rate of today differs from the rate of the line's date.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison was made at the line's date but the posting uses today's rate, so the two need not agree.

edge_cases.outcome: They come in a balanced pair on the same document, so posting them never unbalances it.
